Wider Sports News.title: Allianz to take over HSBC Life Singapore in deal including bancassurance partnership
Wider Sports News.summary: Allianz to take over HSBC Life Singapore in deal including bancassurance partnership Asia Insurance Review
Wider Sports News.body:
Allianz Group (Allianz) and HSBC Holdings (HSBC Group) today announced that Allianz, through its wholly owned subsidiary Allianz Asia Holding, has agreed to acquire HSBC Life Singapore, subject to regulatory approval.

HSBC Life Singapore is a Singapore-incorporated and licensed composite insurer with a strong presence in Singapore’s life and health insurance market. In addition, Allianz and HSBC Bank (Singapore) (HSBC Singapore) have agreed on a 15-year exclusive distribution partnership under which Allianz will provide protection, health, retirement and wealth solutions to HSBC’s customers in Singapore. The partnership builds on a well-established distribution relationship between Allianz and HSBC Group across Asia, and is expected to commence upon completion of the transaction.

Wider Sports News.title: TNT Sports adapts Olympic broadcast playbook to transform Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
Wider Sports News.summary: TNT Sports has ended the BBC's stranglehold on the Commonwealth Games. WBD Sports Europe EVP Scott Young tells SportsPro about how it will use its Olympic creative and technical experience to make the Commonwealth Games a major streaming event. The post TNT Sports adapts Olympic broadcast playbook to transform Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
TNT Sports’ acquisition of the exclusive UK broadcast rights to the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games caught many by surprise when it was announced last December. The BBC had aired the quadrennial multi-sport event since television coverage began in 1954, an unbroken streak of 72 years, and blanket free-to-air (FTA) coverage has allowed previous UK-based Games in Manchester (2002), Glasgow (2014) and Birmingham (2022) to become significant cultural events.

The BBC’s inability or unwillingness to beat TNT Sports’ bid was viewed either as evidence of financial pressures facing the public service broadcaster (PSB) or the reduced appeal of a scaled back Commonwealth Games when compared to previous years, necessitated by the withdrawal of original host Victoria three years ago.

Wider Sports News.title: How Glasgow 2026 plans to save the Commonwealth Games
Wider Sports News.summary: Victoria’s withdrawal as host three years ago didn’t just threaten the 2026 Commonwealth Games, it jeopardised its very existence. Commonwealth Sport chief executive Katie Sadleir explains how a leaner, more efficient hosting model will futureproof the event for decades to come. The post How Glasgow 2026 plans to save the Commonwealth Games appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
The Commonwealth Games are nothing if not adaptable. They began life as the British Empire Games back in 1930 when Britain sought to strengthen cultural ties with its colonies as its formal control weakened.

However, decolonisation was not the death knell for the movement that it should have been and the Commonwealth instead became a global platform for members who might be crowded out in the United Nations or the International Olympic Committee (IOC).

Wider Sports News.body:
Independent communications agency Mutant has been appointed for two sporting events in Singapore: the Singapore Tennis Open (STO) 2026 and HSBC SVNS Singapore 2027, a leg of the World Rugby Sevens Series. The appointments continue Mutant’s partnership with The Kallang.

The agency previously worked on STO in 2024 and HSBC SVNS Singapore in 2023. The appointments follow Mutant’s expansion into MICE and live events capabilities. “Singapore is punching above its weight as a destination for world-class sporting events, and we’re proud to be part of what makes them land well,” said Lina Marican, Regional Managing Director, Mutant.

Wider Sports News.title: Little Dot Studios unveils HyperLaunch to supercharge YouTube revenue and scale channel growth
Wider Sports News.summary: The new tool marks the formal introduction of ‘Little Dot OS’ (Optimisation Sidekicks), the company's proprietary technology suite designed to maximise returns. The post Little Dot Studios unveils HyperLaunch to supercharge YouTube revenue and scale channel growth appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Little Dot Studios, the social media agency, digital media network and multi-platform production company, today unveils HyperLaunch, the latest addition to the Little Dot OS (Optimisation Sidekicks), its growing suite of proprietary optimisation technologies. HyperLaunch helps broadcasters, distributors, sports rights holders, brands and content owners rapidly scale their YouTube output, significantly increasing revenue while maintaining premium channel management standards.

Developed entirely in-house, Little Dot OS leverages over 13 years of expertise managing 1,000+ YouTube channels for more than 600 global partners. Over the past decade, the company has delivered more than half a billion US dollars in revenue for its partners. With HyperLaunch, partners now stand to, on average, triple their historical returns by efficiently monetising vast content archives that were previously too complex or costly to exploit.

Rugby.title: Report: Moana Pasifika's Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa tipped to make All Blacks squad
Rugby.summary: Uncapped Moana Pasifika forward Semisi Tupou Ta'eiloa has been tipped to make the All Blacks squad according to a report.
Rugby.body:
Uncapped Moana Pasifika forward Semisi Tupou Ta’eiloa has been tipped to make the All Blacks squad according to a report. The 23-year-old blockbusting No.8 is likely to be picked according to New Zealand news outlet The Post, with a report suggesting that he will make the 44-man group after signing with NZR.

Ta’eiloa was one of the most destructive ball carriers in Super Rugby Pacific this season, finishing in the top 10 for most carries and top 10 for defenders beaten. His new deal until the end of 2028 with NZR makes him eligible for selection with his physical ball carrying adding another dimension to the loose forward crops.

Rugby.summary: Springboks lock Eben Etzebeth is under pressure to retain his place in the top Springbok side after a long stint of the sidelines.
Rugby.body:
Springboks lock Eben Etzebeth is under pressure to retain his place in the top Springbok side after a long stint of the sidelines according to former Springbok coach Nick Mallett.

Rugby.title: All Black great Ma'a Nonu leaves Toulon for new role at South African club
Rugby.summary: All Black great Ma'a Nonu will join South African club Hollywood Bet Sharks after finishing his second stint with Top 14 club Toulon.
Rugby.body:
All Black great Ma’a Nonu will join South African club Hollywood Bet Sharks after finishing his second stint with Top 14 club Toulon. South African media have floated the idea of Nonu taking the field should Springbok midfielder Andre Esterhuizen be called up by the Boks.

“Ma’a Nonu will spend the next few months in Durban as part of a high-performance mentorship programme designed to accelerate the development of the club’s next generation of players by exposing them to one of the most successful leaders in world rugby,” the Sharks said.

Rugby.title: Channel Islands score six tries to beat Poland
Rugby.summary: The Channel Islands rugby union team beat Poland 38-27 in their second annual "international" match.
Rugby.body:
The Channel Islands rugby union team beat Poland 38-27 in their second annual "international" match. Jack McFarlane crossed in the left corner to give the hosts a ninth-minute lead, but two Dan Tomanek penalties saw Poland go 6-5 up after 16 minutes.

Anthony Armstrong went over on the right wing to put the islands 10-6 up midway through the first half. Charlie Wilkinson was mauled over shortly before half-time after Polish prop Peet Vorster had been sent to the sin-bin.

Rugby.title: Fissler Confidential: James O'Connor deal close; French points-machine in big demand
Rugby.summary: James O’Connor is understood to be set to return to Western Force to finish his career where it began, when he became the youngest-ever Super Rugby debutant at 17 in 2008.
Rugby.body:
James O’Connor is understood to be set to return to Western Force to finish his career where it began, when he became the youngest-ever Super Rugby debutant at 17 in 2008. The veteran Wallaby, who spent last season with Leicester Tigers, had been linked with one of his former club’s Queensland Reds, the NSW Waratahs and United Rugby Championship outfit the Sharks, since it was announced that he was leaving Welford Road.

He picked up the Western Force ‘Rookie of the Year’ award in 2009, winning the first of his Wallabies caps while at the club, where he spent three seasons before moving to the Melbourne Rebels, but his career is set to come full circle.
Rugby.copy:

Rugby.title: Eight possible bolters for the All Blacks' 44-man squad to tour South Africa
Rugby.summary: The others, though, are up for debate, with the coaching staff weighing up whether to go for a 6-4 split of forwards to backs, or 7-3, as discussed last week in Auckland.
Rugby.body:
On Monday, July 27, All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie will name his 44-man squad to travel on the Greatest Rivalry Tour of South Africa. Next month’s tour, which includes four games against South African domestic sides and four Tests, the last of which is in Baltimore, will be a proper litmus test of where Rennie’s side are, less than a year out from the Rugby World Cup in Australia.

The All Blacks got through the three Nations Championship July fixtures without major injury, with Codie Taylor’s calf strain the only concern ahead of the tour. Assuming the 34-man squad are fit and available, Rennie will add ten players to the Nations Championship group to travel to South Africa.

Rugby.title: 'South Africa can widen the All Blacks' previously unseen faultlines'
Rugby.summary: While Dave Rennie made a positive start to his tenure as New Zealand head coach, a Test series in South Africa will expose any weakness.
Rugby.body:
It’s a little dramatic and cliched but there is no other way to frame what lies ahead as the All Blacks’ moment of truth. Having won three successive July Tests under new coach Dave Rennie, the All Blacks now face an eight-game tour of South Africa featuring four matches against the Stormers, Sharks, Bulls and Lions, and four Tests against the Springboks – three in the Republic and one in Baltimore, USA.

The tour is being marketed under the tagline The Greatest Rivalry and is the focal point of the 2026 season. It’s a nostalgic throwback and a test-the-waters play to see if there is fan appetite for an old-fashioned tour of this nature.

Rugby.title: New investment talks ongoing says Gloucester CEO
Rugby.summary: Gloucester chief executive officer Alex Brown says there are talks ongoing regarding new investment in the Prem club.
Rugby.body:
Gloucester chief executive officer Alex Brown says there are "talks ongoing" about new investment in the Prem club. The Cherry and Whites' most recent set of accounts, for the year to June 2025, showed an increase in losses from £516,355 to £2.91m.

"There is interest in Gloucester Rugby but our shareholders and board are very sensitive to who that investment might be," Brown told BBC Radio Gloucestershire. "It has to be right for the club, for the future and we'll take every opportunity that comes but there are talks going on about further investment."

Rugby.title: ACLs, clutches and non-contact: How Grace Deane is preparing for her second Leicester season
Rugby.summary: If there is a moment in her life that Grace Deane hasn’t filled with something worthwhile, then it is likely to be a surprise to those who know her best.
Rugby.body:
If there is a moment in her life that Grace Deane hasn’t filled with something worthwhile, then it is likely to be a surprise to those who know her best. The Leicester Tigers wing is about to embark on her second season at Mattioli Woods Welford Road, and there is plenty on her plate to juggle before the season starts in September.

The 26-year-olds priority is to complete her return to full fitness after she suffered an Anterior Cruciate Ligament [ACL] injury after only three matches for Tigers in 2025/26. She has been able to join in with most of the training sessions since preseason started but crucially isn’t allowed to take part in the contact sessions for now.

Rugby.title: Layla Sae: 'I am going to make the most of it when I do get back'
Rugby.summary: Just 16 minutes into Layla Sae's Harlequins and Premiership Women's Rugby debut last November she was tackled and heard a pop in her knee.
Rugby.body:
Just 16 minutes into Layla Sae’s Harlequins and Premiership Women’s Rugby debut last November she was tackled and heard a pop in her knee. The New Zealand international got back to her feet and tried to continue but she was taken off and later told she had a grade three ACL tear.

Sae’s first reaction to the news was shock and she was “gutted”. Because just a week after relocating to London, alongside international teammate Liana Mikaele-Tu’u, her PWR journey was over.

Rugby.body:
The Monaco Rugby Federation’s U18 team was crowned European runners-up last weekend in Budapest, securing promotion to the Championship, the highest division of European rugby sevens. This historic achievement puts Monaco among the 12 best nations in European U18 rugby sevens.

Only one year after winning the Trophy 2 title to earn promotion to Trophy 1, the young team claimed a silver medal in Hungary. Following a strong tournament, the team was beaten only by Latvia in the final. Despite not claiming the title, Monaco still secured promotion to the Championship alongside Latvia.

Rugby.body:
Gloucester Rugby CEO Alex Brown says talks are ‘ongoing’ to bring desperately needed fresh investment into the club, after a loss of £2.91 million was reported for the 2024/25 financial year.

While Brown says some of the losses – up from £516,000 the year before – can be attributed to ‘accounting nuances’ around the way academy license payments are made, there are fears that unless they can find a new backer, the Cherry and Whites will be left behind their English rivals.

Rugby.title: Ex-All Black captain Todd Blackadder replaced as head coach of Toshiba
Rugby.summary: Former All Blacks captain Todd Blackadder's long reign as head coach of Toshiba Brave Lupus is over, with the 54-year-old being moved 'upstairs' by the Fuchu-based team.
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks captain Todd Blackadder’s long reign as head coach of Toshiba Brave Lupus is over, with the 54-year-old being moved ‘upstairs’ by the Fuchu-based team. Having been appointed in April 2019, Blackadder was one of the longest-serving head coaches in Japan’s Rugby League One, but Brave Lupus have opted to change their coaching team following a disappointing season.

Blackadder led Brave Lupus to back-to-back titles in 2024 and 2025 but they fell short of completing a three-peat in 2026, exiting the competition at the quarter-final stage after an injury-disrupted campaign.

Rugby.title: Antonio Prim on taking Portugal to new heights with historic Nations Cup wins
Rugby.summary: Prop Antonio Prim, 23, says Os Lobos seek to be groundbreakers, elevating Portuguese rugby to places it's never been before.
Rugby.body:
Rapidly improving Portugal has a clear brief about its goals in international rugby. Prop Antonio Prim, 23, says Os Lobos seek to be groundbreakers, elevating Portuguese rugby to places it’s never been before.

Giddy heights were reached at the 2023 Rugby World Cup when Portugal stunned Fiji 24-23. But by 2025, progress had stalled after a record 106-7 loss to Ireland. Earlier this month, Portugal ended their recent World Rugby Nations Cup campaign with an upset 32-28 victory over Tonga in Winnipeg. It was their first win over Tonga and came a week after beating Canada 38-14, following a narrow 30-29 loss to the USA.

Rugby.title: Blues re-sign 'well-respected leader' Taufa Funaki
Rugby.summary: The Blues have locked down halfback Taufa Funaki on a new two-year deal in their latest off-season move.
Rugby.body:
The Blues have locked down halfback Taufa Funaki on a new two-year deal in their latest off-season move. Funaki has played 42 games for his hometown team, with seven tries. A Sacred Heart College product, the 25-year-old former New Zealand U20 player’s signature comes as the club loses stalwart Sam Nock after 11 seasons representing the City of Sails.

Funaki was a big contributor to the drought-breaking 2024 Super Rugby Pacific title run, and says he is excited to return for another two seasons. “I grew up in Auckland dreaming of wearing the Blues jersey, so to be able to continue that journey and keep representing the 09 is something I’m grateful for,” he said.

Rugby.title: Saracens appoint Coetzee as new chief executive
Rugby.summary: Premiership side Saracens appoint South African Ed Coetzee as their new chief executive officer following similar roles at Brive and Sharks.
Rugby.body:
Prem Rugby side Saracens have appointed former Sharks and Bayonne prop Ed Coetzee as the club's new chief executive officer. The 46-year-old made more than 300 appearances in professional rugby, playing four seasons for the Sharks in South Africa, before six years in France at Bayonne and Biarritz.

He then moved into administration, becoming commercial and marketing director at Sharks before taking over as chief operating officer (COO) and then CEO in 2019. Coetzee has been CEO at Brive since 2024, and replaces Charlie Beall who stepped down at the StoneX stadium at the end of the 2025-26 season.

Rugby.title: Springboks fans have never been humble
Rugby.summary: Springboks fans have never been humble... A few years ago, Henry Pollock told me that he wanted to be “spoken about as a great of the game”.
Rugby.body:
A few years ago, Henry Pollock told me that he wanted to be “spoken about as a great of the game”. He explained that one goal was simply an opportunity to move the posts further back. Winning a junior World Cup, making his international debut, beating New Zealand, lifting the Webb Ellis Cup and being named World Player of the Year were all merely “stepping stones”.

Imagine the response if Pollock had actually said any of that. Picture the frothing replies, the bulging veins, the sudden concern for endangered values of rugby. Who does this blond English child think he is? Someone should wipe that smirk off his face.

Rugby.title: RFU introduce toolkit to combat sexism and misogyny at community clubs
Rugby.summary: The Rugby Football Union have partnered with Women in Sport to launch a landmark anti-sexism and misogyny policy to make the sport more inclusive for women's and girls.
Rugby.body:
The Rugby Football Union have partnered with Women in Sport to launch a landmark anti-sexism and misogyny policy to make the sport more inclusive for women’s and girls. Research conducted by the two parties, which included the feedback of over 600 volunteers associated with community clubs in England, have highlighted the scale of sexism and misogyny in the sport at grassroots level.

Quantitative and qualitative evidence gathered from volunteers across the 2025/26 season found that 83 per cent of female respondents had experienced sexism, while a quarter of female match officials reported that they had frequently experienced or witnessed sexist behaviour.

Rugby.title: 'My words had impact': How Laura Delgado is finding her feet in full-time coaching
Rugby.summary: Tuesday 30 June 2026. A day that I will never forget. The day that I became a full-time coach.
Rugby.body:
Tuesday 30 June 2026. A day that I will never forget. The day that I became a full-time coach. 48 hours before arriving in the USA, I was playing for the Barbarians in my last official game at Allianz Stadium. I shared the locker room with so many friends and colleagues. After the game, I went to the Harlequins cottages to get my things and boarded the plane, my destination set for Minneapolis, to join Women’s Elite Rugby’s Twin Cities Gemini as an assistant.

It was an intense start to this new adventure. I headed straight to practice after arriving. The girls were incredible from the get-go. However, I have to say it was weird to be involved in a training session without being a player. After so many years working on my skills, honing my scrummaging abilities, I was there to solely coach and help players become better.

Rugby.title: Argentina's Albornoz charged following altercation with match officials
Rugby.summary: Argentina's flyhalf Tomás Albornoz has been issued with misconduct charges following his side's close 31-24 loss to England at Estadio Único Madre de Ciudades.
Rugby.body:
Argentina’s flyhalf Tomás Albornoz has been issued with misconduct charges following his side’s close 31-24 loss to England at Estadio Único Madre de Ciudades. World Rugby confirmed that Albornoz that the flyhalf will face a hearing for his conduct after the final whistle which saw an altercation with referee Angus Gardner.

After consultation with the TMO, a potential late try to Bautista Delguy was overturned leading to an emotionally charged ending. Albornoz will be the first player to be adjudicated under the new Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, which was agreed at the recent Shape of the Game forum.

Queensland Reds enforcer Lukhan Salakaia-Loto is back in the mix for the Wallabies, with new coach Les Kiss also including one potential debutant in a 34-man squad ahead of two Tests against Eddie Jones’ Japan next month.

It’s a new era for the Wallabies, with Kiss now set to lead the side through to Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027 on home soil. Rugby Australia announced 450 days ago exactly that Kiss would be the successor to Joe Schmidt, who led the side in 31 Tests.

Rugby.title: James O’Connor opens up on South African move that almost happened
Rugby.summary: James O’Connor did consider a move to South Africa, with reports linking the 64-Test Wallaby to URC outfit the Sharks.
Rugby.body:
James O’Connor did consider a move to South Africa, with reports linking the 64-Test Wallaby to URC outfit the Sharks. But ‘JOC’ has decided to stay put in Australia, revealing some exciting personal news after returning home.

O’Connor has been heavily linked with a surprise move to the Durban-based outfit, following a season with the Leicester Tigers. The backline utility has previously enjoyed overseas stints with another English side, with a France Top 14 powerhouse, and a New Zealand juggernaut.

Rugby.title: Jorja Miller feels she's 'just scraping the surface' as she re-signs beyond Olympics
Rugby.summary: A superstar of both the Sevens and fifteens formats, Jorja Miller has extended her contract with New Zealand Rugby through to 2029.
Rugby.body:
A superstar of both the Sevens and fifteens formats, Jorja Miller has extended her contract with New Zealand Rugby through to 2029. Still just 22 years old and already an Olympic gold medallist, two-time SVNS Series champion, a two-time World Rugby Sevens Player of the Year and the youngest Kelvin R. Tremain Memorial Player of the Year since Jonah Lomu, Miller says she’s as hungry as ever to take the next step in her career, adamant she’s got plenty more room to grow.

Explaining her decision to re-sign beyond the 2028 Olympics, Miller shared her lofty goals in the sport. “I feel like I’m still just scraping the surface, and I don’t feel like I’ve reached my potential of the best I can be, so I’ll continue to strive to be better as a teammate and as a leader and in whatever role I’m doing,” she said.

Rugby.title: Joe Schmidt bows out on a high
Rugby.summary: The coach steps aside having made admirable progress across Australian rugby, but there is much to be done ahead of a home World Cup.
Rugby.body:
Twilight is the time when day meets night and the light blends with the dark. Earth’s atmosphere disperses scattered shards of sunshine, and the world exists in a state of partial illumination. That is where the Wallabies are right now, living in the twilight zone. There is some light, but not enough to create a new dawn.

The definition of ‘success’ depends on the start point of the venture. When Eddie Jones was installed as head coach of England after a disastrous home World Cup in 2015, paradoxically he inherited a squad primed to succeed. The Red Rose promptly embarked upon an 18-match unbeaten run, and that became the foundation stone for the best win record in English coaching history.

Rugby.title: Guinness World record attempt in Sandbach aims to smash Rugby Sevens for mental health charity
Rugby.summary: Guinness World record attempt in Sandbach aims to smash Rugby Sevens for mental health charity Sandbach Nub News
Rugby.body:
Ex-England and Saracens forward, George Kruis, joins local men's and women's rugby players in Sandbach on Friday (24 July) to set a world record. There will be a Guinness World Record attempt for the longest games of men's and women's Rugby Sevens at Sandbach RUFC in Bradwall Road to raise money for rugby mental health charity, LooseHeadz.

The current men's record stands at 24hrs 30mins, while the women's record has never been attempted. The record attempts will start at midday on Friday, with the new records hopefully established on Saturday mid-afternoon.

Rugby.title: England star Noah Caluori vows to come back 'stronger' after undergoing surgery
Rugby.summary: The winger's stock continues to rise after he scored on his England debut against Fiji in the Nations Championship.
Rugby.body:
Noah Caluori has revealed that he spent most of last season playing with an injury, which has now been rectified following surgery. One of the rising stars of English rugby, Caluori posted a pictured of himself lying in a hospital bed with his right forearm in a cast on his Instagram account, while giving fans a reassuring thumbs up.

The picture was accompanied by an upbeat message from the winger, whose stock continues to rise after he scored on his England debut against Fiji in the Nations Championship. Caluori wrote: “Surgery done. Been playing with this injury for 8 months now. Gonna be working hard to get back stronger then (sic) before.”

Rugby.title: Brain injury cases should be thrown out, High Court told
Rugby.summary: Lawyers for rugby's governing bodies argue the absence of medical documents should lead to hundreds of brain injury cases being dismissed.
Rugby.body:
The High Court has been told that hundreds of cases in rugby's multi-million-pound concussion legal action should be thrown out. Players from both codes of the sport claim that the authorities failed to put safeguards in place to protect them from the consequences of repeated head impacts.

World Rugby, the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU), Rugby Football Union (RFU) and Rugby Football League (RFL) deny breaching a duty of care to protect the players from injury. Lawyers representing the governing bodies have argued that claims should be thrown out due to documents surrounding the neurological testing process not being disclosed, which they claim is a breach of a 2024 court order.

Rugby.title: Exclusive: Bordeaux Begles to compete in London rugby sevens tournament
Rugby.summary: Exclusive: Bordeaux Begles to compete in London rugby sevens tournament City AM
Rugby.body:
Investec Champions Cup winners Bordeaux Begles will send a team to the London City 7s in a major coup for the Square Mile tournament. The showstopping French Top 14 outfit, who in May won their second consecutive European title, will participate in the second edition of the London sevens tournament, which takes place in September at the Honourable Artillery Company.

Last year’s event was won by London club Harlequins, who beat Saracens in the final, but this year will have an international flair with Bordeaux Begles joining the roster. The outfit – which features a range of domestic French and wider international stars – beat Leinster to lift their second European trophy two months ago.

Rugby.title: PWR champion and Olympian swaps Saracens for Exeter Chiefs
Rugby.summary: Deborah Wills has traded Saracens for Exeter Chiefs ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Deborah Wills has traded Saracens for Exeter Chiefs ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season. The 35-year-old had two spells in North London, the most recent of which being a one season stay for the 2025/26 campaign as Saracens won the PWR Cup and league. Last season Wills made eight appearances and scored one try.

Wills spent the better part of a decade playing elite rugby sevens after finding rugby aged 21. She spent numerous seasons on the HSBC SVNS Series, won a Commonwealth Games bronze medal in 2018 and represented Team GB at the 2020 Olympic Games in Tokyo.

Rugby.title: Scarratt joins England coaching team permanently
Rugby.summary: England's record points-scorer Emily Scarratt commits her long-term future to the Red Roses coaching team.
Rugby.body:
England's record points-scorer Emily Scarratt has committed her long-term future to the Red Roses coaching team. The 36-year-old joined John Mitchell's side on an interim basis as the lead attack and backs coach for this year's Women's Six Nations.

Following England clinching their eighth successive Women's Six Nations title in May, Scarratt returned to her role as assistant coach at Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) side Loughborough Lightning.

Rugby.title: 'I'm proud to be part of the journey': Scarratt signs on for more as Red Roses assistant
Rugby.summary: Two-time Women's Rugby World Cup winner Emily Scarratt has joined John Mitchell's Red Roses coaching staff on a full-time basis.
Rugby.body:
Two-time Women’s Rugby World Cup winner Emily Scarratt has joined John Mitchell’s Red Roses coaching staff on a full-time basis. Scarratt, 36, led England’s attack on an interim basis at the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations and helped the team to a fifth Grand Slam in a row in May. Across this year’s Women’s Six Nations, England scored 283 points – 27 more than their total the previous year.

The former 119-cap international has signed on as attack coach for the entirety of the next Women’s Rugby World Cup cycle. The Red Roses’ next fixtures will come in the WXV Global Series, when they host Australia, Canada and New Zealand in September, prior to two Tests against Canada and one against the USA Women’s Eagles on the road in October.

Rugby.title: Boks release 5 from squad ahead of Argentina and Greatest Rivalry Tests
Rugby.summary: Rassie Erasmus has named a streamlined squad of 43 players ahead of the upcoming Tests against Argentina and New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
Springboks boss Rassie Erasmus has named a streamlined squad of 43 players ahead of the upcoming Tests against Argentina and New Zealand, the latter forming ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’ (RGR) series.

The group, which has been cut by five, will assemble in Johannesburg on Sunday to start preparing for the Test aaginst Los Pumas in Buenos Aires on August 8. The Springboks will then face the All Blacks in four Tests – at Ellis Park in Johannesburg (22 August), the DHL Stadium in Cape Town (29 August), FNB Stadium in Johannesburg (5 September), and the M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore, USA (12 September).

Rugby.title: Pamela Santos: 'I kept working and believing that I would get there'
Rugby.summary: How many times would you be willing to go to a national team camp, not get selected to play, go back home and wait for another chance?
Rugby.body:
How many times would you be willing to go to a national team camp, not get selected to play, go back home and wait for another chance? Most would say a handful of times; a few potentially would say for a couple of years, but no one would be available to go for it for over half a decade.

Well, almost not everyone, with Brazilian prop Pâmela dos Santos Soares being the exception. After enduring six years of unsuccessful attempts, she finally made the cut and became a full-fledged Yara.

Rugby.title: 'Rugged and robust, like the country it represents': Scotland ditch heather jersey
Rugby.summary: Scotland have ditched their heather-coloured away strip in favour of a more traditional white version for the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Scotland have ditched their controversial heather away strip in favour of a more traditional alternative white kit for the 2026/27 season. The heather strip was introduced in September 2022 and divided opinion among Scotland supporters, with many wrongly believing it to be pink in colour.

It doesn’t take much for users of X to get shirty and the social media platform was awash with negative comments when it was launched. “Rooted in the topographical make-up of the country, the white kit is embellished with Scotland’s wild mountain terrain, a nod to its 282 Munros and thousands of lesser peaks that run from the south-west of Stranraer to the Shetland Islands and all the rugged land between,” Scottish Rugby explained.

Rugby.title: 2026 Swyftx Super Rugby Women's Grand Final preview
Rugby.summary: When it comes to Super Rugby Women’s history, no rivalry has been more hotly contested than the New South Wales Waratahs and the Fijian Drua.
Rugby.body:
When it comes to Super Rugby Women’s history, no rivalry has been more hotly contested than the New South Wales Waratahs and the Fijian Drua. The two teams are now set to meet in a first-ever final played on the islands.

Both sides have taken very different journeys to get to the big dance, the Drua bounced back from their opening round 42-29 loss to the Waratahs in Sydney to build into the season and eventually topped the table.

Rugby.title: Kenyan Rugby Union confirms overhaul of National Sevens Circuit div two
Rugby.summary: The tournament is now set to feature six legs running from July to September, taking place in Kisumu, Nairobi, Mombasa and Embu.
Rugby.body:
The National Sevens Circuit is set to see further changes ahead of the 2026 season, with the Kenyan Rugby Union (KRU) confirming an overhaul of the Division Two format of the competition.

The 2026 series of the circuit is already set to look markedly different, off increased investment into the competition that will see an additional Sh 34.14 million (AUD$382,000) in funding, double the amount invested in 2025.

Rugby.title: All Blacks legend weighs into Ireland: 'They've turned into a pack of whingers'
Rugby.summary: Justin Marshall has let rip on the latest episode of The Good, The Bad and The Rugby, ANZ, after Ireland were beaten 40-21 by New Zealand at Eden Park last Saturday.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks legend Justin Marshall says Ireland should take a long, hard look at themselves rather than look for excuses after they were beaten 40-21 by New Zealand in the third round of the Nations Championship last weekend.

Defensively Ireland were all over the shop in the first half as they trailed 28-7 at half-time before restoring some pride to ‘win’ the second half. The match could possibly have had a different outcome had Luke Jacobson’s dangerous clearout at the ruck on 27 minutes been upgraded to a red, while Quinn Tupaea was perceived to be lucky not to get binned for a deliberate knock on.

Rugby.summary: In an unprecedented era of success, it has also come with individual recognition.
Rugby.body:
Following their victories over the weekend both in the 2026 World Rugby Junior World Championship and in the Nations Championship against Wales, South African Rugby finds itself in an envious position.

Combined with back-to-back Rugby World Cups with it’s senior men’s side, the Rainbow Nation can now boast back-to-back championships in the Junior World Championships and back-to-back championships in the HSBC SVNS World Series earlier in June.

Rugby.title: Why the Springboks' rush defence won't bother the All Blacks
Rugby.summary: On the Boks' defence not being what it once was, the Springboks conceded five tries and 31 points to the Barbarians, three tries and 21 points to England, and four tries and 28 points to Scotland.
Rugby.body:
Former Springboks lock Victor Matfield is confident that the Springboks will bring their “aggressive defence” on the edges for the All Blacks, and that New Zealand hasn’t yet faced a defence like this so far in 2026.

Matfield said it’s been “easy” against passive defences for the All Blacks, and that the Springboks’ rush defence will be “up there” in their faces. “The one thing they haven’t been able to consistently get right is to play against this rush defence and, again, they haven’t faced it so far this year, so it’s nicer going to the outside channels,” he told John Kirwan on the Rivals podcast.

Rugby.title: Marco Riccioni learns his fate after unusual red card
Rugby.summary: The first red card of Marco Riccioni's 39-cap Test career has earned the tight-head a two-match ban.
Rugby.body:
Italian international Marco Riccioni will miss two matches for his new club Perpignan after being dismissed for his part in a touchline scuffle during Italy’s thumping 57-10 defeat to Australia last weekend.

Riccioni, who’d started the match and been replaced on 54 minutes, got involved in a mass brawl as it spilled over the touchline close to the replacements bench and was promptly shown the red card by referee Christophe Ridley.

Rugby.body:
Here we go again. Another head coach is stepping into the hot seat for the Wallabies, with Les Kiss taking over ahead of Men’s Rugby World Cup 2027. The new boss is the fourth Wallabies HC in five and a half years after Dave Rennie, Eddie Jones and Joe Schmidt.

It’s an all-too-familiar feeling for Wallabies fans, who continue to dream of a brighter tomorrow while someone new leads the way. Fans draped in green and gold look ahead to the future with a curious sense of optimism, but there’s plenty of uncertainty that lies ahead.

Rugby.title: Ioane Moananu secures Super Rugby return to New Zealand on two-year deal
Rugby.summary: Moananu enjoyed a breakout season with the Crusaders in 2025, starting six of 12 appearances for the club and scoring five tries as an injury to George Bell kept the All Black sidelined.
Rugby.body:
The Highlanders have brought one of New Zealand’s most damaging hookers back to home soil, signing Ioane Moananu on a two-year deal ahead of the 2027 season. Moananu enjoyed a breakout season with the Crusaders in 2025, starting six of 12 appearances for the club and scoring five tries as an injury to George Bell kept the All Black sidelined. However, there was no room for the then 23-year-old at Rugby Park in 2026 with the promotion of former New Zealand U20 captain Manumaua Letiu to the top squad.

Other Kiwi clubs offered wider training group contracts, meaning Moananu would only play if injuries hit the squad, but the youngster wanted minutes. After finding a 2026 contract at the Waratahs, Moananu was honest about entering the season with a chip on his shoulder, and proceeded to add six tries in eight appearances for the Sydney-based club. He was announced as one of nine departures from Daceyville after the season wrapped, with his future in Super Rugby remaining uncertain.

Rugby.title: 'Boks will come with the same game plan': Schalk Burger predicts Wellington repeat for All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Former Springboks flanker Schalk Burger has predicted that South Africa will replicate their Welllington game plan when they face the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
Former Springboks flanker Schalk Burger has predicted that South Africa will replicate their Wellington game plan when they face the All Blacks in next month’s Test series. After losing 24-17 to the All Blacks at Eden Park, the Springboks flipped the script with a new-look line-up and returned to beat the All Blacks 43-10 in Wellington the following week.

Key to the dominant win was the aerial supremacy by the Springboks, using the high ball through Mannie Libbok to put the home side under pressure repeatedly. Burger highlighted that throughout July, none of the All Blacks’ opponents tested them out through the air effectively.

Rugby.title: 'Farrell wants Ireland to be the best
Rugby.summary: Ireland's coach has a little over a year to restore Ireland's status near the summit of the international game.
Rugby.body:
Through a Nations Championship prism, Ireland did reasonably in their first ever southern hemisphere swing. They landed the vital punch in a slobber-knocker against Australia, handed out three Test debuts in a much-changed XV and outlasted Japan, and were left to rue gift-wrapping to New Zealand tries in an Eden Park loss.

Taking in a wider view – one that includes the 2027 World Cup – there are plenty of reasons to be fretful. For a while, it was hard to tell exactly where Ireland stood in world rugby. In the past season alone, there had been uncomfortable losses to New Zealand, South Africa and France, but a record home win over Australia, securing a Triple Crown by taking down a dangerous Scottish side, and that emphatic Twickenham victory over England.

Rugby.title: RFU aim to 'maximise opportunities' with women's performance calendar alignment
Rugby.summary: Major women's rugby stakeholders have put the development of its players first with an alignment of the women's performance rugby union calendar ahead of the 2026/27 season.
Rugby.body:
Major women’s rugby stakeholders have put the development of its players first with an alignment of the women’s performance rugby union calendar ahead of the 2026/27 season. The Rugby Football Union, Premiership Women’s Rugby, BUCS and Celtic Challenge have collaborated to align the performance rugby union calendar across international domestic seasons to further support player experience and progression.

A detailed Under-23 review found that players moved across numerous environments, balancing club, university and international commitments. It is hoped this alignment of the performance calendar can give players, coaches, clubs and universities “greater clarity” and allow players to “focus on performing, developing and enjoying rugby, rather than managing competing demands on their time”.

Rugby.title: England report card: All 28 Nations Championship players rated
Rugby.summary: The bar was set pretty low for England heading into the Nations Championship this month – simply, win a rugby match again. Fortunately for their fandom, Steve Borthwick's side are back to winning ways and are starting to rebuild after a hellish Six Nations. It didn't come easily though.
Rugby.body:
The bar was set pretty low for England heading into the Nations Championship this month – simply, win a rugby match again. Fortunately for their fandom, Steve Borthwick’s side are back to winning ways and are starting to rebuild after a hellish Six Nations. It didn’t come easily though.

After a manhandling at the hands of the world champions in round one, their fifth Test loss in a row, England returned to winning ways the following week against a Fiji side that looked more like 15 blokes on the third day of a stag do. They backed it up in round three against Argentina in a game which exhibited the best and worst of England, where each passage of play seemed to last only long enough for referee Angus Gardner to draw breath before blowing his whistle for yet another English infringement.

Rugby.title: Luke Jacobson might be the jack of all trades and master of none
Rugby.summary: The most surprising selection sprung by Dave Rennie and his selectors this July was picking Chiefs captain Luke Jacobson as the starting openside.
Rugby.body:
The most surprising selection sprung by Dave Rennie and his selectors this July was picking Chiefs captain Luke Jacobson as the starting openside. Heading into the first Test, many expected Ardie Savea to remain in the No.7 jersey, with a host of popular No.8 options available in Peter Lakai, Wallace Sititi and even Jacobson himself.

But Savea has been picked as the No.8 in every Test and Jacobson has remained the first choice No.7 since week one, a configuration not many saw coming. The Chiefs captain has managed 27 Tests since his debut in 2019, with just 13 of them in the starting side. His career to date has been taking a backseat to the likes of Dalton Papalii, Sam Cane, and Ardie Savea, with most of his appearances coming from the bench. Even last November he was on the bench for the All Blacks XV, a long way off starting for the top side.

Other than that, New Zealand’s 40-21 win over Ireland was pretty meritorious. I don’t think Ireland are especially good and, for all my reservations about whether the All Blacks’ unbeaten run at Eden Park is important, it clearly matters to the other team.

Rugby.title: Wallabies' game-by-game review for Nations Championship July series
Rugby.summary: Last time the Wallabies played Ireland alone, they had a 67% success rate at the lineout, which is a massive turnaround with comparatively rookie locks.
Rugby.body:
The Nations Championship ended on a high for the Wallabies and their fans, but this series must go down in the history books as a failure. Two wins from the three Test matches was the widely accepted bar throughout Australia, and the Wallabies were very close to achieving this.

While the series as a whole must be deemed as coming up short on the ambitions and realistic goals both internally and externally, there are positives to take out of the July Tests as a whole.

Rugby.summary: Reg Tayler is making the step up from assistant coach to the top job with the Australia Women’s Sevens program ahead of the 2028 LA Olympics.
Rugby.body:
Reg Tayler is making the step up from assistant coach to the top job with the Australia Women’s Sevens program ahead of the 2028 LA Olympics, with Rugby Australia confirming on Tuesday the successor to former boss Tim Walsh.

Rugby.title: The key behind Quinn Tupaea and Jordie Barrett's growing chemistry
Rugby.summary: The Chiefs midfielder was dropped after the first Nations Championship Test against France in Christchurch, being replaced by Hurricanes centre Billy Proctor.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea has described the growth of his combination with Jordie Barrett since the first three Test matches under head coach Dave Rennie. Tupaea and Barrett played in the No.12 and No.13 jerseys in 2025 under former head coach Scott Robertson, before starting the France and Ireland Tests in those same positions in 2026.

The Chiefs midfielder was dropped after the first Nations Championship Test against France in Christchurch, being replaced by Hurricanes centre Billy Proctor. Rennie then opted for the Tupaea-Barrett combination for the all-important Ireland Test at Eden Park on Saturday, where the two seemed to combine more effectively than in previous outings.

Rugby.title: Will Jordan makes more try-scoring history with ‘freebie’ against Ireland
Rugby.summary: Will Jordan can’t stop scoring for the All Blacks, making the most of “a freebie” in a 40-21 win over Ireland at Eden Park.
Rugby.body:
Will Jordan can’t stop scoring for the All Blacks, making the most of “a freebie” in a 40-21 win over Ireland at Eden Park. Those five points now see Jordan stand alone in the history books, becoming the first New Zealander to reach the 51-try tally.

Black Ferns great Portia Woodman-Wickliffe was the first New Zealander across women’s and men’s international rugby to score 50 career tries, with the winger racing away for a historic five-pointer during the 2025 Rugby World Cup.

Rugby.title: Earl wants changes to 'brutal' Nations Championship format
Rugby.summary: Ben Earl calls for a change to the Nations Championship format after England's "brutal" schedule in the summer leg of the inaugural competition.
Rugby.body:
Ben Earl has called for a change to the Nations Championship format after England's "brutal" schedule in the summer leg of the inaugural competition. England had to play three Tests in three different continents on successive weekends and accumulated 25,000 miles of travel.

Victory over Argentina on Saturday keeps Steve Borthwick's team in the hunt for a place in the final on 29 November at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium. However, four long haul and four short haul flights in the past four weeks have contributed to players losing sleep and a reduced training schedule.

Rugby.title: Joe Schmidt leaves the Wallabies in a far better place
Rugby.summary: Joe Schmidt has improved Australian rugby on and off the field, but it remains to be seen what new coach Les Kiss will do with his legacy.
Rugby.body:
The Joe Schmidt era has ended the way it started: comfortably beating a team which has caused the Wallabies more than a few headaches in previous years. In 2024, Schmidt opened his Wallabies account with wins over Wales in Sydney and Melbourne, after the Welsh ended Australia’s disastrous 2023 Rugby World Cup campaign, and Eddie Jones’ troubled return to the top job in the process.

So after Italy beat Australia in Florence in 2022, and again in Udine last season, there were plenty reasons for Wallabies fans to be nervous about the final game of the Schmidt reign.

Rugby.title: Ambitious Carpenter commits to Sale long-term
Rugby.summary: Sale full-back Joe Carpenter extends his contract with the Sharks until 2029.
Rugby.body:
Sale full-back Joe Carpenter has extended his contract with the Sharks until 2029 with the aim of landing the silverware that has proved so elusive in recent seasons. The 24-year-old, who made his England debut last July against the USA, had one year remaining on his deal but has signed on for more, confident that last season's seventh-place Prem finish was a blip.

"I'm absolutely buzzing to be committing my future to this club," said Carpenter. "It's a club and a group that I cherish in so many different ways and one that I truly believe will achieve something special in the near future.

Rugby.title: Contest or no contest? The eternal struggle between the Springboks and All Blacks
Rugby.summary: As Dave Rennie's new attacking ethos takes shape, Rassie Erasmus wants to ensure the grunt and skill of a true set-piece battle does not wane.
Rugby.body:
When rugby union finally bit the bullet and turned professional on 26th August 1995, it was trending exactly 100 years behind rugby league, which had first rounded the same corner back in 1895. The underlying connection between the two codes still informs the game as it approaches its 31st anniversary as a professional sport.

League did away with lineouts and the scrums are strictly symbolic, just another way to restart the game with all the forwards in one place. There is no contest for the ball permitted either during or after the tackle. A change of possession is only mandated by law after a six-tackle ‘set’ has been completed. The game is less complex and a lot easier to referee than its cousin.

Rugby.title: Ireland report card: All 34 Nations Championship players rated
Rugby.summary: Ireland emerged from an inaugural Nations Championship campaign with two wins from three, beating Australia and Japan before falling short against New Zealand at Eden Park.
Rugby.body:
Ireland emerged from an inaugural Nations Championship campaign with two wins from three, beating Australia and Japan before falling short against New Zealand at Eden Park. There were positives to leave Andy Farrell encouraged: Joe McCarthy’s physical authority, Hugo Keenan’s return to form and the emergence of Nick Timoney and Sean Jansen offer a succession plan in the back-row.

Yet familiar concerns remain. The lineout malfunctioned far too often, the scrum could charitably be described as barely competent, and several senior figures looked like a summer off would have done them the world of good.

Rugby.title: Mick Cleary: 'There was plenty to admire in England’s showing, even if the madcap finish scrambled many minds.'
Rugby.summary: Steve Borthwick brought to a close an inconsistent season with a helter-skelter Test and just about emerged victorious
Rugby.body:
The Sound of Silence, music to the ears of Steve Borthwick. If only the soundtrack of a subdued away stadium could play for ever and a day for the England head coach. But it didn’t last in the match itself as England came perishingly close to following their footballing counterparts and throwing the result late on. Nor have the critical murmurings been completely stilled at Twickenham as England’s long summer labours come to an end, a grafting, initially uplifting, performance yielding Borthwick’s men their first victory on the road in a year. As Thomas Tuchel discovered when boos greeted his name being announced at the Bronze match in Miami, the relationship with a support base can be a delicate affair, yet Borthwick, with two wins from three Nations Championship matches, can afford to rest, recuperate and plan ahead. But, despite 25,000 miles travelled over the last three weeks, England have somehow managed to take only half a step forward. If only they could bottle their first half display and put it out on the field for the full 80.

Their dynamic, purposeful opening salvo in Santiago del Estero showed the potential that is there. But it remains a half-built edifice. One puff of turbulence and panic set in. Admittedly, it’s dangerous to read too much into press conferences but the manner in which Borthwick snapped at his critics when questioned about the towering tally on England yellow cards, four in this match to take the haul to 14 across the last ten tests, indicates the strain he’s been under. The line of inquiry is wholly legitimate. England will not advance to the upper echelons of the world game unless they tighten their discipline. But fair enough. Borthwick has been under pressure. And rightly so after England’s worst Six Nations for eons and a thumping defeat in Johannesburg on the opening Nations weekend. Credit where it is due though. This was a match that had to be won. And, for all the misgivings, it was.

Rugby.title: Newcastle Red Bulls agree to new signing u-turn
Rugby.summary: After careful consideration, Newcastle Red Bulls have agreed to release Joji Nasova from his contract for next season.
Rugby.body:
After careful consideration, Newcastle Red Bulls have agreed to release Joji Nasova from his contract for next season, for personal reasons. The Fijian, capped in 15s and sevens, had agreed terms to join the club ahead of the 2026/27 campaign. However, the 26-year-old will not move to the Gallagher PREM and will remain with his current team, Fijian Drua.

In a press release, Newcastle said: “The club has worked constructively with the player, Fijian Drua and the Fiji Rugby Players Association to reach a resolution that recognises Joji’s personal circumstances, while also respecting the importance of contractual stability within the RFU and World Rugby frameworks.”

Fijian star Joji Nasova will not be joining Newcastle next season after the Red Bulls agreed to release him from his contract. The 25-year-old wing, who won a sevens silver medal at the Paris Olympics, had signed to move to the ambitious Prem club but will now stay with Fijian Drua.

Rugby.title: SA Rugby statement: Junior Springboks
Rugby.summary: The Junior Springboks have been praised by SA Rugby as they returned to South Africa on Monday after successfully defending the World Rugby U20 Championship title in Georgia.
Rugby.body:
The Junior Springboks have been praised by SA Rugby as they returned to South Africa on Monday after successfully defending the World Rugby Junior World Championship title in Georgia.

South Africa retained the crown with a 16-5 victory over France in Saturday’s final, backing up last year’s triumph in Italy, where they beat New Zealand 23-15. The squad and management were congratulated by South African Rugby Union president Mark Alexander, who praised the team’s courage, discipline and skill throughout the tournament.

Rugby.title: Super Rugby Aupiki: Talking points as Blues and Matatu set up showpiece finale
Rugby.summary: Three teams finished with four wins each in the Super Rugby Aupuki 2026 regular season, but Matatu will host the Blues in the final after securing a bonus point in a thrilling 38-29 last-round loss.
Rugby.body:
Three teams finished with four wins each in the Super Rugby Aupuki 2026 regular season, but Matatu will host the Blues in the final after securing a bonus point in a thrilling 38-29 last-round loss.

The Hurricanes Poua beat Chiefs Manawa 47-33, but the defending champion Blues edged a place in the decider. The last two rounds saw the Poua become the form team and the Blues rediscover their groove. The final of Super Rugby Aupiki will be held next Saturday afternoon at Te Kaha/One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch.

Rugby.summary: Western Force had hooker Hera-Barb Malcolm Heke sin-binned after direct head contact on a Waratahs player in the 19th minute.
Rugby.body:
ormer sevens star Tia Hinds and winger Amelia Whitaker each scored two tries, as NSW Waratahs booked a Super W rugby grand final date with Fijian Drua, with a 33-22 semi-final away win over Western Force.

The Waratahs scored four first-half tries at HBF Park on Saturday to lead 26-0 inside the first 35 minutes. The Force outscored the visitors 22-7 in the rest of the game, recording four tries, but never got the deficit below 11.

Rugby.title: Joe Schmidt's positive outlook on 31-Test Wallabies tenure
Rugby.summary: But only the second Australian success in his last 11 Tests in charge could not completely mask a galling record of just 12 wins from 31 matches during his three-year tenure.
Rugby.body:
He departs with the worst losing strike rate for a Wallabies coach in more than half a century, but Joe Schmidt maintains he has left Australian rugby in better shape. The Wallabies’ 57-10 Nations Championship triumph over Italy on Saturday snapped a six-match losing streak that left even Schmidt “depressed” and hugely frustrated.

The order-restoring victory in Perth may have given fans renewed hope that the eighth-ranked Wallabies can be competitive as home hosts of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Rugby.summary: But without getting ahead of himself, Blair told media in Auckland on Sunday morning that the coaching staff felt their side produced some "really pleasing stuff" against Ireland.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair has assessed his side’s attack after three Tests under Dave Rennie, before the squad jets off to South Africa for the Greatest Rivalry Tour.

The All Blacks have made it clear with their recent performances that a counter-attacking, free-flowing style is at the forefront of their new attacking blueprint. Rennie and his coaching staff, including Scotland-born Mike Blair, whose portfolio consists of looking after the All Blacks attack, have injected what feels like new life into the highly-skilled group of outside backs.

Rugby.title: Wales closing the gap to world's best
Rugby.summary: Jac Morgan is confident Wales are closing the gap to the best in the world despite another hammering by South Africa in the Nations Championship.
Rugby.body:
Jac Morgan believes Wales are closing the gap to the best sides in the world despite chastening Nations Championship defeats by Argentina and South Africa. Steve Tandy's side enjoyed a 39-24 victory over Fiji in the opening round in Cardiff but then suffered comprehensive losses to the Pumas and Springboks.

The world champions rotated their side for the round three fixture, giving debuts to four players, but still eased to a seven-try 43-0 win. The Springboks would have challenged their 73-0 November win in Cardiff were it not for errors in the 22, but Morgan insists Wales are closing the gap to the big hitters.

The former Moana Pasifika head coach is the designated “defence coach” in the All Blacks setup, while Neil Barnes, Jason Ryan, and Mike Blair also assist Rennie in other areas.

The All Blacks’ defence has been a huge talking point during Rennie’s short tenure to date, but Rennie said he was happy with the shifts the group have made in the short time together.

The Vern Cotter-coached side will gain the veteran’s services at the same club he made his professional debut at, back in 2017, where he played 17 games across two seasons.

Perese then made his Wallabies debut against Scotland back in 2021, going on to make five more appearances in the green-and-gold. The outside back has played for Bayonne in the French Top 14, the Waratahs, and most recently, for the Leicester Tigers.

Rugby.summary: England signed off their July tour with a deserved 31-24 victory over Argentina in Santiago del Estero.
Rugby.body:
England signed off their July tour with a deserved 31-24 victory over Argentina in Santiago del Estero. Here, the Press Association looks at five things learned from the ‘Southern Series’ of the Nations Championship.

A 25,000-mile odyssey taking in three continents produced a solid return of two wins from three Tests despite a brutal schedule that poses the question as to why the Rugby Football Union agreed to send its stars on four long haul plus four short haul flights in the space of three weeks.

Rugby.summary: Fin Smith admits England must urgently stamp out their discipline problems if they are to fulfil their aspiration of becoming a major force on the world stage.
Rugby.body:
Fin Smith admits England must urgently stamp out their discipline problems if they are to fulfil their aspiration of becoming a major force on the world stage. Steve Borthwick’s team lifted their total of yellow cards for 2026 to 15 in eight Tests after being shown four more in Saturday’s chaotic 31-24 victory over Argentina in Santiago del Estero.

They also lost the penalty count 15-6 and conceded a penalty try yet, despite the second-half meltdown that twice left them playing with 13 men, they had the resolve to deliver a triumphant climax to their July tour.

Tennis.body:
Chasing her dream of becoming a world tennis champion, teen athlete Maristella Torrecampo and her father took a gruelling 13-hour bus from her sleepy hillside hometown for her latest match in Manila.

Tennis.title: 10 top tennis stars to miss US Open as Emma Raducanu decision made
Tennis.summary: 10 top tennis stars to miss US Open as Emma Raducanu decision made Daily Express
Tennis.body:
The entry list for the upcoming US Open has been released and some big names will be missing. It comes after some high-profile withdrawals from Wimbledon, where world No.3 Carlos Alcaraz was missing from the men’s draw and Emma Raducanu pulled out on the women’s side on the eve of the tournament. Action from Flushing Meadows will begin less than a month from now and British fans will be keen to learn whether 2021 champion Raducanu will take her place in the field.

For now, the 23-year-old is there. However, she has not played since losing the Queen’s final to Donna Vekic. “I’ve done everything possible to try to get to the start line tomorrow but after a final scan tonight, the niggle I’ve been managing has developed into a stress fracture and I’ve been medically advised to stop pushing through,” she said the day before the Wimbledon first round. “Playing at Wimbledon, in front of a home crowd, means everything to me, so this is really difficult to process. I want to thank you all for your support and encouragement. Especially at a time like this, it is invaluable. I look forward to seeing you when I’m back.”

Tennis.body:

Tennis.body:
Jack Draper has received support from Andy Murray ahead of his latest comeback from injury next week. Former British number one Draper had enlisted the help of three-time grand slam champion Murray as a coach for the grass court season, but after a successful run to the last four of an ATP event in Eastbourne, the 24-year-old was forced to pull out of Wimbledon.

A recurrence of bone bruising in Draper’s left arm denied him the chance to play at his home major and appeared set to end his brief coaching relationship with Murray, but the retired Scottish player has joined his British compatriot in America to boost his upcoming return to action.

Tennis.title: Serena Williams' former coach predicts if Emma Raducanu will ever win another Grand Slam title
Tennis.summary: Serena Williams' former coach predicts if Emma Raducanu will ever win another Grand Slam title Tennishead
Tennis.body:
Emma Raducanu has not been close to repeating her Grand Slam title win in the past five years. Raducanu won the US Open in 2021, becoming the first qualifier in history to win a major singles title.

The Briton has not added to her Grand Slam triumph since then, with Raducanu currently out due to a stress fracture in her lower right leg. As Raducanu races to be fit for this year’s US Open, Serena Williams’ former coach, Rick Macci, has predicted if the 23-year-old can win another major title.

After all, whilst there is talent to be found amongst the likes of Emma Raducanu, Cam Norrie and Katie Boulter, none really feel like they are ready to challenge the sport’s very best on the biggest stages.

Jack Draper, at Indian Wells no less, more than reinforced his credentials in this department when he beat the likes of Ben Shelton, Taylor Fritz, Joao Fonseca, Holger Rune and Carlos Alcaraz en route to his maiden Masters 1000 title.

Tennis.title: Jack Draper misses out on 2026 US Open main draw as former semi-finalist set to enter qualifying
Tennis.summary: Jack Draper misses out on 2026 US Open main draw as former semi-finalist set to enter qualifying Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Former British No 1 Jack Draper is set to have to qualify for the US Open this year as the 2024 semi-finalist missed out on a spot in the main draw. Draper is poised to return to action at the DC Open in Washington from July 27 after missing Wimbledon due to a recurrence of bone bruising in his left arm.

The injury was the latest blow for the 24-year-old, who has managed only a handful of tournaments since first stepping away from the tour a year ago with the same issue. Draper's ranking has taken a hit as a result, dropping down to 147th in the world, resulting in him having to likely qualify in order to play the fourth and final Grand Slam of the season.

Tennis.title: Nearly one year after reaching No.4, Jack Draper begins rebuild from Challenger level
Tennis.summary: Nearly one year after reaching No.4, Jack Draper begins rebuild from Challenger level Yardbarker
Tennis.body:
Just a year after reaching the ATP Top 5, Jack Draper is facing one of the biggest rebuilding challenges of his career. The Briton has entered the Brownsburg Challenger, scheduled for August 10-16, as he looks to recover his ranking, confidence and competitive rhythm after a difficult period marked by injuries.

Draper’s presence at Challenger level would have been almost impossible to imagine months ago. The 24-year-old was one of the biggest rising stars in tennis, reaching a career-high No. 4 ranking and becoming a Grand Slam semifinalist before physical setbacks interrupted the momentum of a breakthrough period.

Tennis.title: How Asian brands build global rosters, one deal at a time
Tennis.summary: How Asian brands build global rosters, one deal at a time Sporting Goods Intelligence Europe
Tennis.body:
A widening roster of basketball and tennis signings, from Stephen Curry and Nikola Jokic to Kyrie Irving, Emma Navarro and Emma Raducanu, shows Anta, Li-Ning, 361 Degrees, Uniqlo and Asics building signature shoes, co-designed lines and ambassador programs across North America and Europe.

When Dwyane Wade walked away from Nike’s Jordan Brand for Li-Ning in 2012, the sports business press treated it as a curiosity, a wealthy Chinese company buying a name it could not otherwise earn (The New York Times, October 2012). Fourteen years later, that move looks less like an anomaly and more like the opening move of a strategy that has since scaled across three Chinese companies, two Japanese ones, and dozens of athletes spanning basketball, tennis and football.

Tennis.title: WTA: Tour announces mandatory SRY gene test for players to determine their sex in order to compete
Tennis.summary: WTA: Tour announces mandatory SRY gene test for players to determine their sex in order to compete Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
The WTA has announced that tennis players will have to undergo genetic sex testing to play on the women's tour. In an update to its eligibility policy, the WTA confirmed that athletes will have to undergo a one-time test for the SRY gene, which determines biological sex, coming into effect on Tuesday, with players facing disciplinary action should they refuse testing.

Previous WTA rules allowed the participation of transgender women provided their declared gender was female and they maintained a lower testosterone level for two years before competing.

Tennis.title: Players will need sex test to play on WTA Tour
Tennis.summary: The Women's Tennis Association is to ask all players to undergo genetic sex testing in order to compete on the WTA Tour.
Tennis.body:
The Women's Tennis Association (WTA) is to require all players to undergo genetic sex testing in order to compete on the WTA Tour. In the latest edition of its women's eligibility policy, which will come into effect on Tuesday, players will be required to provide a cheek swab, blood or saliva sample to test for the presence of the SRY gene which is part of the Y chromosome and causes male characteristics to develop.

Players will be tested just once in their lifetime and only a negative result, showing no presence of the gene, will permit them to compete on the Tour. If they test positive, players will face further medical assessment before being allowed to play.

Golf.title: 5 suggestions for optimal practice without getting lessons
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel shares five suggestions for getting the most out of your practice — without taking lessons. The post 5 suggestions for optimal practice without getting lessons appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I have the opportunity to watch golfers of all skill levels on the practice range. As an instructor, my teaching eye naturally scans the swings as players try to launch that little ball into the air and keep it straight.

It’s always fun to watch someone celebrate a great shot. What’s a little harder to watch is seeing the same mistake repeated over and over without any adjustment, often relying on hand-eye coordination or luck rather than sound technique.

Golf.title: Ryo Ishikawa used to be Blades Brown. He sees something different in golf's current teen star
Golf.summary: Ryo Ishikawa once walked in Blades Brown's shoes. But golf's former phenom sees something different in its current teen star. The post Ryo Ishikawa used to be Blades Brown. He sees something different in golf’s current teen star appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Seventeen years ago, Ryo Ishikawa made his PGA Tour debut. He was a 17-year-old global golf phenom who had already won on the Japan Tour and appeared to be headed to the top of the golf world. He first won on the Japan Tour at age 15, finished T20 at the Masters at 19 and was a top-50 player in the world at age 20.

Every shot Ryo Ishikawa hit and every second of his lengthy post-round press conferences were broadcast. Nicknamed “The Bashful Prince,” Ishikawa was expected to become a golf superstar. But as is often the case, golf had other plans. Ishikawa was a PGA Tour staple from 2012 to 2017. He had two runner-up finishes, nine top 10s and made more cuts than he missed. But he never found the winner’s circle, and a back injury led to a dip in play that caused him to lose his PGA Tour card in 2017. Ishikawa returned to the Japan Tour and rebuilt his body and his game. He now has 20 career wins on the Japan Tour and is playing as a full-time Korn Ferry Tour member this year as he looks to return to the PGA Tour for the first time in a decade.

Golf.title: With LIV Golf facing 'headwinds,' former major champ plans for new future
Golf.summary: Graeme McDowell knows that LIV is facing "headwinds" as it tries to secure a future after 2026. With that in mind, he's making other plans. The post With LIV Golf facing ‘headwinds,’ former major champ plans for new future appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf is running out of time, and Graeme McDowell is among the pros planning for an alternative golf future. Ever since the Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund announced it would cease backing the breakaway league after 2026, LIV Golf has been trying to create a new future. But this week at LIV Golf U.K., all the talk has suggested that it’s getting late for the rebel outfit.

Earlier this week, Martin Kaymer told Today’s Golfer that the LIV Golf team event in Michigan is “highly unlikely” to be played. Jon Rahm said he was “optimistic” LIV would have a future past 2026 but wouldn’t give any specific reason for his optimism apart from saying he’s optimistic by nature. LIV Golf was dealt another blow earlier in the week when the Asian Tour, which had been a partner of LIV since its launch, agreed to a deal with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour.

Golf.title: Living on a prayer: Has LIV Golf drawn its final breath in the UK?
Golf.summary: Living on a prayer: Has LIV Golf drawn its final breath in the UK? The Observer
Golf.body:
So this is how it ends, Calvin Harris tunes wafting across undulating Staffordshire countryside while Rome burns. Barring intervention by someone with both a fetish for burning the GDP of a minor nation and the ability to do so, these are the last days of LIV Golf, its British leg likely the third from last.

For all they self-identify as revolutionaries, LIV UK feels strikingly similar to any other professional golf event. You can buy overpriced gyros and lukewarm lager and filthy, naughty fries – fries that are frankly begging for it. Their fan village resembles any other; children’s games sponsored by corporations expediting humanity’s demise. The obvious addition is the music, obnoxiously blasted across most tees and greens, with players choosing their own walk-on themes, meaning Tyrell Hatton emerges to “I just want relief from my stress” from NF’s My Stress. It’s unclear what any of this adds, manufactured and forced hype adding little to an atmosphere which still seems remarkably golfy. Nobody appears to be enjoying themselves more because some mumble rap is being played slightly too loud. The only place this isn’t true is the 14th, a par three flanked by two stands called The Birdie Shack, the most darts-ified area, blaring Sweet Caroline and John Denver. Between groups, an indefatigable hypeman oversees a mini-game between members of a stag party, incoherently drunk but sober enough to chip footballs into undersized goals from 12 feet or so. Chase and Status are performing after play on Saturday, because of course they are. Equally, the noise isn’t constant or unavoidable – at one point I set myself on a particularly comfortable hillock beside the fifth for a breather and, the enduring professional that I am, having returned from the World Cup on Monday, woke up 20 minutes later.

Golf.title: Herbert Leads LIV Golf UK by Four With Nine Holes to Play
Golf.summary: Herbert Leads LIV Golf UK by Four With Nine Holes to Play golfpost.com
Golf.body:
Lucas Herbert is on the verge of making history at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB, holding a four-shot lead over Bryson DeChambeau as he heads into the back nine of Round 3 at JCB Golf & Country Club in Rocester, Staffordshire. Should the 30-year-old Australian close out Sunday's final round from the front, it would mark his second wire-to-wire victory of the 2026 LIV Golf season.

Herbert arrived at the Staffordshire venue in fine form, having spoken of carrying momentum from The Open the previous week, and he wasted no time stamping his authority on the field. His opening 61 — nine birdies and an eagle, bogey-free — shattered the course record at JCB Golf & Country Club, which had previously stood at 62. "If you were going to pick days you were going to shoot 59, I wouldn't have thought today would've been the day," he said. "The golf course is a little firm...a bit of breeze out there kind of moved around. I'm pretty incredibly happy with 61."

Golf.summary: Nick Faldo: This is the REAL reason LIV Golf failed Today's Golfer
Golf.body:
He’s been one of LIV Golf’s strongest critics since its inauguration, but Sir Nick Faldo isn’t here to kick the failing league while it’s down. Though he will say ‘I told you so’…

Sir Nick Faldo leans back in his chair as he recalls his thoughts from the early days of LIV Golf. “The oversell was just flat-out BS,” he smiles. “Greg Norman said, ‘We’re going to supercharge the excitement of golf!’ And I said, ‘It’s golf, for crying out loud.’ Golf is chess in the field.”

Golf.title: "I wanted to carry on": LIV Golf UK leader Lucas Herbert on keeping Jarrod Lyle's legacy alive
Golf.summary: "I wanted to carry on": LIV Golf UK leader Lucas Herbert on keeping Jarrod Lyle's legacy alive Golfmagic
Golf.body:
Lucas Herbert opened up on the impact Jarrod Lyle had on his life after taking a commanding lead of LIV Golf UK at the halfway stage. Lyle was an Australian professional golfer who battled leukaemia in his teenage years while pursuing a PGA Tour career.

Lyle never won on the PGA Tour but recorded two victories on the Korn Ferry Tour before his passing, with one of the most memorable moments of his career coming with a hole-in-one during the 2011 WM Phoenix Open at TPC Scottsdale.

Golf.title: Chasing historic 59, Michael Kim knew exactly how to handle the moment
Golf.summary: Michael Kim shot 59 to etch his name into the record books at the 3M Open on Friday, recording the 16th sub-60 round in PGA Tour history. The post Chasing historic 59, Michael Kim knew exactly how to handle the moment appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — Sometimes, it behoves players to not think about the big picture. One shot at a time. Lots of golf left. Don’t look at the leaderboard. That sort of thing. A couple of weeks ago at the Evian Championship, Haeran Ryu tallied up her scorecard on the 18th green and was shocked when she realized she shot 60, the lowest major round in women’s golf history.

But as for Michael Kim? He knew exactly where he stood on Friday. The 33-year-old, world No. 57 torched TPC Twin Cities, never made a bogey and birdied his last four to shoot a 12-under 59 — just the 16th sub-60 score in PGA Tour history. At 14 under, he leads the 3M Open with the afternoon wave still to finish.

Golf.title: Kim feels 'pretty cool' after carding historic 59
Golf.summary: Michael Kim is thrilled to be "part of the history books" after a superb 12-under par round of 59 at the 3M Open in Minnesota.
Golf.body:
Michael Kim is thrilled to be "part of the history books" after a superb 12-under-par round of 59 at the 3M Open in Minnesota. The American drained a 24-foot birdie putt at the final hole to post just the 16th sub-60 round ever on the US PGA Tour.

Kim birdied the last four holes at TPC Twin Cities course in Blaine, lifting both arms in triumph when the putt on 18 rolled in before unleashing a mighty fist-pump. The 33-year-old had 12 birdies without a bogey to finish his second round in the lead, three shots in front of compatriot Ben Kohles.
