His no-nonsense pre-shot routine and rapid pace of play are refreshing qualities for a pro golfer in an age where overthinking and over-analysis routinely lead to five-hour rounds, all while his unorthodox (yet highly effective) swing has caught everyone’s attention.

After watching the Kiwi claim the Claret Jug last weekend, I got to thinking about four factors that undoubtedly helped him on his quest to become a major champion. Check them out below and apply them to your own game. They may just help you shoot lower scores.

Golf.title: This putting aid hones your stroke — and mimics real-life lip-outs
Golf.summary: PuttOUT's Premium Pressure Putt Trainer features a circular target the size of a regulation hole, with tapered sides to mimic lip-outs. The post This putting aid hones your stroke — and mimics real-life lip-outs appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There’s no question that the fastest way to lower scores is by minimizing wasted shots on and around the green. And for players at every level, putting is often to blame when a hole — or round — goes sideways.

Think about it this way: In a regulation round, you’re expected to hit around 14 drives, 22 or so shots with shorter clubs … and 36 putts! So if you’re looking to shave a few strokes from your score, putting is the most obvious area to focus on.

Golf.title: Bettinardi turns the tables on the zero torque trend with new Hexperimental release
Golf.summary: Bettinardi is flipping the script on the putter market and turning one of their 'zero torque' Antidote shapes into a traditional hosel. The post Bettinardi turns the tables on the zero torque trend with new Hexperimental release appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Today’s putter market has been flooded with “zero torque” offerings. Earlier this year Bettinardi added more options to the market with 2 Hexperimental shapes, but this time they’re flipping the script. The new Bettinardi Hexperimental #2 adapts the high M.O.I. ‘Simply Balanced’ Antidote SB2 shape and converts it into traditional heel-shafted setup without “zero torque” technology.

“We’ve had a wide range of players in our Tour Department, from pros to elite amateurs, fall in love with the Antidote SB2, but zero-torque isn’t for everyone,” said Sam Bettinardi, president of Bettinardi Golf. “That’s exactly the gap the Hexperimental #2 was designed to fill.”

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau misses the point as he directly addresses Open Championship controversy at LIV UK
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau misses the point as he directly addresses Open Championship controversy at LIV UK hitc.com
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau bounced back well from the controversy he caused at The Open Championship last week with a round of 64 on day one at LIV Golf UK. DeChambeau was right in the mix to win The Open after he made a birdie on his final hole of the day on Friday to put him one shot adrift of the leader, Lucas Herbert.

However, within minutes of leaving the 18th green at Royal Birkdale, he was informed that he had broken rule 8.1a on the fifth hole. Bryson DeChambeau was penalized two strokes by Open officials after he was deemed to have improved the playing area around his ball in the rough during his second round.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau ends media blackout: "I was passionate about what I believed"
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau ends media blackout: "I was passionate about what I believed" Golfmagic
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has spoken publicly for the first time since he was assessed a two-shot penalty during the second round of The Open at Royal Birkdale. DeChambeau, 32, was docked two strokes after Friday's second round he was judged to have inadvertently improved his swing path on the fifth hole before playing his second shot.

R&A officials said DeChambeau broke the rules by trampling down knee-high rough behind his ball. A furious DeChambeau mulled withdrawing from the final men's major of the year and even threatened to get US president Donald Trump involved in proceedings when he was informed of the penalty after walking off the 18th green.

Golf.title: ‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him Open
Golf.summary: ‘Two holes and I’m there for the Claret Jug’: DeChambeau says two-shot penalty cost him Open The Guardian
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been “right there for the Claret Jug” if he had not received a two-shot penalty in the Open Championship last week at Royal Birkdale. DeChambeau made a positive start to last week’s tournament after opening with a 67 and then a 66 on Friday, but his second-round score was later adjusted to 68 after he was handed a retrospective two-stroke penalty at the 5th hole after a video review. The 32-year-old was punished after match officials ruled he had improved the area of his backswing by standing on and flattening some long grass.

DeChambeau was in the mix at the top of the leaderboard but he dropped from second to fifth in the standings after his bogey was subsequently turned into a triple bogey. The American protested against the decision and even threatened to pull out of the tournament, but he played through the weekend and made 69 in the third round before a final-day 72.

Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau responds to controversial penalty at The Open: ‘I thought I was right’ The Independent
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has said he is “moving past” the controversial two-shot penalty that hampered his bid for The Open at Royal Birkdale. DeChambeau was docked two shots after his second round in Southport having been deemed by officials to have improved the area of his backswing by standing on and flattening grass as he played a shot out of the rough on the fifth hole.

The 32-year-old has since been accused of attempting to involve Donald Trump in the rules dispute, and eventually faded from contention to finish in a tie for 14th at the year’s final men’s major.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been in Open contention without penalty
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been in Open contention without penalty The Herald
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau believes he would have been “right there for the Claret Jug” if he had not received a two-shot penalty in The Open Championship last week at Royal Birkdale. DeChambeau made a positive start to last week’s tournament after opening with a 67 and then a 66 on Friday, but his second-round score was later adjusted to 68 after he was handed a retrospective two-stroke penalty at the fifth hole.

The 32-year-old was punished after match officials ruled he had improved the area of his backswing by standing on and flattening some long grass after a video review. DeChambeau was in the mix at the top of the leaderboard, but he dropped from second to fifth in the standings after his bogey was subsequently turned into a triple bogey.

Golf.title: Ryder Cup icon bellows at Bryson DeChambeau after nearly being hit by drive
Golf.summary: Ryder Cup icon bellows at Bryson DeChambeau after nearly being hit by drive The Sun
Golf.body:
BRYSON DeCHAMBEAU nearly hit Ian Poulter with a ball after a rogue tee shot at LIV Golf UK on Thursday. The pair were both playing their first round at the JCB Golf and Country Club when disaster almost struck.

Ryder Cup legend Poulter, 50, was lining up a shot on the seventh hole fairway when he turned in fear. Just as the Brit started to go into his stance, he backed away and put a hand to his head after a ball flashed past his vision.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau addresses 'adversity' at Open Championship
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau spoke to assembled media for the first time since his controversial two-stroke penalty at the Open Championship. The post Bryson DeChambeau addresses ‘adversity’ at Open Championship appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau, following Thursday’s first round of LIV Golf’s U.K. event, spoke to assembled media for the first time since his controversial Open Championship penalty — and touched briefly on the hoopla surrounding his much-scrutinized tie for 14th at Royal Birkdale.

DeChambeau opened with a round of eight-under par at JCB Country Club, the second-best score of the day. Afterward, he spoke to reporters for the first time since before the Open, where he’d declined to provide media availability.

Golf.title: Herbert shoots 61, leads DeChambeau by 3; Ripper with 4-shot team lead at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB
Golf.summary: Herbert shoots 61, leads DeChambeau by 3; Ripper with 4-shot team lead at LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB LIV Golf
Golf.body:
ROCESTER, England – Fresh off his career-best finish in a major, Lucas Herbert continued that momentum into Thursday’s opening round at LIV Golf United Kingdom Presented by JCB. In the process, he produced another career-best – a bogey-free 11-under 61, his lowest-ever round relative to par.

“First time I’ve had 11, so that’s kind of cool,” Herbert said. “That’s a fun one.” Definitely fun for the Ripper GC star, as he grabbed a three-shot lead at JCB Golf & Country Club after producing a round with nine birdies and an eagle. His closest pursuer is Crushers GC Captain Bryson DeChambeau, who shot an 8-under 64 that included a stretch of four consecutive birdies and another stretch of three straight birdies to go with his eagle at the par-5 sixth.

Golf.title: Scottie Scheffler gets little things right in surprise 3M Open debut
Golf.summary: Scottie Scheffler's putter betrayed him at the Open Championship, but it was hot during a stellar first day at the 3M Open on Thursday. The post Scottie Scheffler gets little things right in surprise 3M Open debut appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — As a Minnesotan — me, the author of this article — I can assure you Scottie Scheffler has done all of the right things in the Land of 10,000 Lakes this week. He went downtown with his family and stopped at a local coffee shop on Monday (we’re big on stimulating the urban economy), signed every autograph after his practice round on Tuesday and complimented fans on Wednesday.

“A few people that recognized me were very nice,” Scheffler said on Wednesday, about his Monday adventure into Minneapolis. “They asked for photos. I was with my family so I said ‘No, not right now.’ They didn’t make a face, or they were kind of like, No, no, I totally understand, thanks for being here. I was kind of taken back by how nice people have been so far.”

Golf.title: 7 things you're getting wrong about your Handicap Index
Golf.summary: The Handicap Index, designed to level the game's playing field, is golf's most useful metric. It's also widely misunderstood. We explain. The post 7 things you’re getting wrong about your Handicap Index appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
What’s your handicap? And do you know what it actually measures? A lot of golfers don’t. The game’s most useful metric is also one of its most misunderstood. Misconceptions abound about everything from the calculations behind what’s officially known as a Handicap Index to what those numbers represent.

Here are seven of the most common myths, clarified. (Don’t have a handicap? You can sign up for one here.) Myth No. 1: My Handicap Index is my average score Nope. Your Handicap Index isn’t based on your average round. It’s calculated using the eight best of your most recent 20 Score Differentials. It’s designed to reflect your playing potential — not what you typically shoot on a Saturday morning.

Golf.title: Ryan Fox partied hard after The Open. Then things got awkward
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox partied all night after winning the Open Championship, then wound up at the airport with the guy he'd just beat. The post Ryan Fox partied hard after The Open. Then things got awkward appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ryan Fox took all of 22 seconds to read and roll in the birdie putt that clinched the Open Championship. But his celebration lasted a good deal longer. Fresh off a victory that transformed him into a fast-playing fan favorite, the 2026 Champion Golfer of the Year joined GOLF’s Subpar podcast to recount the revelry that followed at Royal Birkdale — a party that stretched well into Monday morning — and the notable airport encounter that came after.

Fox said the festivities began upstairs in the players’ lounge, where he and his entourage poured red wine into the Claret Jug and drank from the famous trophy, pausing only when tournament obligations called.

Ian Poulter admitted Bryson DeChambeau was "not at fault at all" after revealing the American's tee shot "just grazed" past his ear during a frightening incident in the opening round of LIV Golf UK.

Golf.title: Ryan Fox wasted no time hitting his Open-winning putt. Here's why
Golf.summary: On this week's episode of Subpar, newly-minted Open champion Ryan Fox explained why it only took 22 seconds for him to hit his winning putt. The post Ryan Fox wasted no time hitting his Open-winning putt. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ryan Fox won his maiden major championship in impressive fashion on Sunday at Royal Birkdale, birdieing four of his final six holes, including the 18th, where he hit a masterful approach to 11 feet and then drained the putt to claim the Open title by a single shot over clubhouse leader Cameron Young.

One of the most notable details of Fox’s final hole was the way he wasted no time over his life-changing putt. In fact, it took only 22 seconds after Fox’s playing partner, Sam Burns, tapped in for his par for Fox to send his winning putt on its way to the hole.

Golf.title: Here’s the prize money payout for each golfer at the 2026 LIV Golf United Kingdom event
Golf.summary: Here’s the prize money payout for each golfer at the 2026 LIV Golf United Kingdom event Golf Digest
Golf.body:
It’s been a while since we’ve seen LIV Golf in action and there have been plenty of headlines in the meantime. The last event was in early June and how the league is back this week with its event in the United Kingdom at JCB Golf & Country Club in Staffordshire, England. The usual cast will, for now, play for the overall $30 million purse with the winner taking home $4 million and the winning team splitting $3 million.

LIV Golf’s top draw, Bryson DeChambeau, was the biggest newsmaker last week at the British Open at Royal Birkdale, despite not winning. His rules fiasco late Friday was a sight to behold. But he’s in England looking for his third victory this season after wins in Singapore and South Africa. He’s second in the season-long standings behind Jon Rahm, who has won this year in Hong Kong and Mexico City but has been more consistent. Rahm can wrap up the individual season title if he wins and DeChambeau finishes in a three-way tie for second place or worse.

Golf.title: ‘Could be de-greened’: Charley Hull hits 15-foot putt, then plays 5 more shots
Golf.summary: Charley Hull putted for a birdie during the first round of the ISPS Handa Scottish Open. And she finished the hole with a nine. The post ‘Could be de-greened’: Charley Hull hits 15-foot putt, then plays 5 more shots appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Charley Hull, one day before this week’s ISPS Handa Women’s Scottish Open, described what is required to succeed in links golf. She said she felt she was starting to become more comfortable with the style.

“If you look at like the British Open,” Hull said, “there’s a lot of elements in it, and like British Opens always have like so many different kind of winners. “So I feel like there is a little bit of luck involved and a lot of patience involved because you can get bad bounces, and you can get — have funky shots and stuff. So you just have to accept them and just kind of just deal with it.”

Golf.body:
Seven LIV Golf players have reportedly told Flushing It they intend to leave the breakaway circuit at the end of the 2026 season, regardless of whether the league secures fresh investment for next year.

The bombshell claim comes amid growing uncertainty over LIV Golf's long-term future after the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF) confirmed earlier this season it will end its financial backing of the league after 2026.

Golf.title: ‘Golf needs rivalries’: Rory McIlroy's former agent believes animosity between Masters champion and Bryson DeChambeau is good for the game
Golf.summary: ‘Golf needs rivalries’: Rory McIlroy's former agent believes animosity between Masters champion and Bryson DeChambeau is good for the game Belfast Telegraph
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy’s recent comments about Bryson DeChambeau at The Open Championship are exactly what golf needs, claims the Holywood star’s former agent Andrew ‘Chubby’ Chandler. McIlroy, in his usual forthright manner, described DeChambeau’s manner as ‘performative’ after the two-time US Open winner was involved in a rules dispute on day two at Royal Birkdale last week.

DeChambeau was assessed a two-stroke penalty for inadvertently improving his lie on the fifth hole, but it was his actions following that which drew McIlroy’s ire, the big-hitting American threatening to withdraw from the tournament in protest while also trying to get US President Donald Trump involved, which delayed the release of the third round tee times.

Golf.title: LIV Golf: Graeme McDowell has held 'positive' talks over DP World Tour return
Golf.summary: LIV Golf: Graeme McDowell has held 'positive' talks over DP World Tour return BBC
Golf.body:
Graeme McDowell says he has held "really positive" talks about returning to the DP World Tour next season and believes he is "fortunate" to have a route back into mainstream competition.

McDowell told BBC Sport that he and the tour have agreed to meet again in November to finalise plans for 2027 amid ongoing uncertainty over LIV Golf's future. The 46-year-old, who joined LIV in 2022, won 11 tournaments on the DP World Tour between 2002 and 2020.

Golf.title: 'I was not informed': H.S. golfer DQ'd from U.S. Junior Am for new rule breach
Golf.summary: High school golfer James Nagle was disqualified from the 2026 U.S. Junior Amateur for multiple breaches of a recently adopted local rule. The post ‘I was not informed’: H.S. golfer DQ’d from U.S. Junior Am for new rule breach appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The 2026 U.S. Junior Amateur has moved on to match play, and so far much of the attention has been on a competitor who narrowly missed out on the final rounds: Charlie Woods. The 17-year-old son of three-time U.S. Junior Am champ Tiger Woods lost in a 14-man playoff on Wednesday for the final two spots in the match-play portion of the event. His effort was made harder by an intrusive camera click from a spectator.

But another competitor, James Nagle, saw his hopes of a U.S. Junior Amateur triumph end much earlier. Rather than a result of his play, Nagle’s exit came in the form of a DQ on Monday, a result of breaching a rare, recently adopted rule.

Golf.title: How Ryan Fox, Shane Lowry, and Nico Echavarria choose their wedge set-ups
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox has a unique steep delivery that required the perfect RTZ grind at Royal Birkdale. Picking wedges is more about you than the ground. The post How Ryan Fox, Shane Lowry, and Nico Echavarria choose their wedge set-ups appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When championship conditions turn baked-out and firm, the knee-jerk reaction among amateur players is to instantly strip bounce off every wedge in the bag. And YES, it did happen a bit last week at Royal Birkdale with players getting low bounce wedge grinds built up “just in case”.

The logic seems sound on paper: tighter lies demand a lower leading edge to prevent the sole from skidding into the middle of the golf ball. On Tour, however, the response from the trucks is far more personal. While firm fairways and tight turf do trigger an influx of low-bounce wedge options across the field, a player’s delivery geometry, swing path, and wrist release play a far larger role in grind selection than ground hardness alone.

Golf.title: LIV's team event on brink of cancellation, per captain Martin Kaymer

Golf.body:
Martin Kaymer, captain of LIV Golf’s Cleeks team, told reporters on Wednesday that it is “highly unlikely” the circuit will stage its August team finale in Michigan. The news was first reported by Ben Parsons of Today’s Golfer, who spoke with a “disappointed” Kaymer ahead of this week’s LIV Golf UK event.

It comes as the embattled league seeks to secure funding for next season following the withdrawal of Saudi support earlier this season. Kaymer said that he expects the next three LIV events — this week in England and subsequent events in New Jersey and Indianapolis — will go ahead as scheduled, but barring a sudden change, the team finale in Michigan, scheduled for the Cardinal at Saint John’s in Plymouth, Mich., won’t happen. (He put the chances at five percent.) An earlier event scheduled for New Orleans was postponed indefinitely.

Golf.body:
Martin Kaymer has cast doubt on LIV's Team Championship season finale going ahead in another blow to the beleaguered Saudi breakaway series. Chief executive Scot O’Neil is leading the search for over €300million of new money after the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia announced it was withdrawing backing at the end of the year after spending almost €4bn since its inception in 2021.

O’Neil spoke to the team captains on Tuesday at this week’s LIV event in Staffordshire and two-time major winner Kaymer said the news was not particularly encouraging. "I know that Indianapolis (the final individual event) is most likely happening. There was a conversation yesterday: Michigan, highly unlikely. According to yesterday, it didn’t look good," he told reporters at the event.

Golf.title: For only $20, you can play this quirky six-time Open Championship site
Golf.summary: Musselburgh Links, a six-time Open site outside Edinburgh, Scotland, sits inside the Musselburgh Racecourse, on its sprawling infield. The post For only $20, you can play this quirky six-time Open Championship site appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I played a new course the other day — that is, new to me — a nine-holer with a bargain-basement green fee and a wide-open tee sheet. It’s in Scotland, outside Edinburgh and inside the Musselburgh Racecourse, on its sprawling, rumpled infield. I had heard people talk about the Musselburgh Links often over the years but finally got to it a couple days after Ryan Fox, get-on-with-it Kiwi golfer, holed his winning putt at the Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. Fox could play this par-34 course, a former Open venue itself, in under an hour. He plays fast and so does this course. When the Scots invented golf they didn’t mean for it to be an all-day activity. (While we’re young, mon — or do your sheep shear themselves?) I imagine the new Open champ would like it. I know Sandy Lyle, winner of the ’85 Open, digs its whole vibe.

Upon arrival I saw no signs for the pro shop or whatever so I walked through an open pathway to the track itself, the red-brick grandstands now behind me, lush grass track ahead. The whole place was pretty much asleep on this warm weekday afternoon, and the whole scene brought to mind a long-ago visit to Doubleday Field in Cooperstown, N.Y., on a still summer day when there was no game.

Golf.title: Aaron Wise is battling more than just the golf course
Golf.summary: Former NCAA champ and PGA Tour Rookie of the Year Aaron Wise left golf to focus on his mental health. Now he's ready to talk about it. The post Aaron Wise is battling more than just the golf course appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
BLAINE, Minn. — Aaron Wise thinks hard before he answers questions. He wants to actually answer them, because he wants you to understand, because he’s spent years trying to make sense of it himself. His press conference at the 3M Open on Wednesday was lengthy and vulnerable and thoughtful. He had a lot to say. But probably because Aaron Wise has had a lot to deal with.

“It’s a constant daily battle out here,” Wise said. Years ago, Wise was one of the brightest young stars on the PGA Tour. He was the 2016 NCAA champion, and as a 21-year-old rookie shattered the scoring record at the 2018 Byron Nelson and won PGA Tour Rookie of the Year. Then, five years later, he withdrew just days before the 2023 Masters to focus on his mental health.

Golf.title: The practice habit that's hurting your golf game without knowing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Monique Thoresz explains why leaving headphones in while practicing could be hurting your game. The post The practice habit that’s hurting your golf game without knowing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
You’ve probably seen it at your local driving range: golfers with headphones in, either taking a phone call or listening to their favorite playlist. Maybe they’re trying to relax, block out distractions, or make practice more enjoyable. While there’s nothing in the Rules of Golf that prohibits listening to music, as a coach, I recommend leaving the headphones in your bag during practice sessions.

Golf is a game that demands concentration. One of the most important skills every player needs to develop is the ability to stay focused despite distractions. On the golf course, you can’t control the conditions. There may be noise from nearby groups, changing weather, unexpected delays, or simply long periods of waiting between shots. Learning to accept those moments instead of trying to eliminate them is an essential part of becoming a better player.

Golf.title: Ryan Fox’s speedy pace was a marvel. Should more golfers step on the gas?
Golf.summary: Watching Ryan Fox motor his way to an Open Championship victory makes you wonder if more golfers wouldn’t benefit from picking up the pace. The post Ryan Fox’s speedy pace was a marvel. Should more golfers step on the gas? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you didn’t see Ryan Fox coming, that might be because relative to many of his grind-it-out, stuck-in-the-mud peers, Fox blazes around the course like a greyhound chasing a hare. Ask Scottie Scheffler, who played alongside Fox and Zecheng Dou in the third round of the Phoenix Open earlier this year — or at least Scheffler thinks he played with Fox. “We walk off the 9th tee, and he goes, ‘Foxy, it doesn’t even feel like you’re in the group,’” the newly minted Champion Golfer of the Year said Sunday evening at Birkdale. “It just feels like we’re playing in a two-ball, you hit it so fast. It’s just in the air.”

Fox has always played with haste, dating back to his teen days in Auckland, New Zealand, when he’d join his father, Grant, a New Zealand rugby great, on corporate golf outings and intentionally waste little time to ensure he wasn’t holding up his playing partners. That Fox processed things quickly — not just on the golf course but also on the cricket pitch and tennis court — also didn’t hurt. See ball, hit ball.

Golf.title: Rahm enters LIV Golf UK on cusp of a three-peat

Golf.body:
ROCESTER, England – Whether it happens this week in the UK or next month in the U.S., Jon Rahm likely will win his third consecutive LIV Golf season-long Individual Championship. Nothing is guaranteed as of now, but it seems inevitable – as inevitable as a top-10 finish whenever Rahm tees it up at a LIV Golf tournament.

Rahm could clinch the three-peat if he wins LIV Golf United Kingdom presented by JCB, provided his closest pursuer, Bryson DeChambeau, doesn’t finish solo second or in a two-way tie for second. If DeChambeau finishes in a three-way tie for second or worse, then Rahm would have enough points going into the final two regular-season tournaments in New York and Indianapolis to clinch the title, no matter what anybody else does.

Golf.title: 2 major pro golf acquisitions just gave us a glimpse into the future
Golf.summary: On an otherwise innocuous Tuesday, two major pro golf announcements provided a glimpse into golf's competitive future. The post 2 major pro golf acquisitions just gave us a glimpse into the future appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Changes to professional golf in the LIV era, while frequent, are about as interesting as bowel movements. I get it because I have also felt my eyes glaze over at a headline capturing the “latest changes.” I get it because I have also wondered when and how much I am supposed to care about the smallest shifts in corporate governance and marketing budgets. I get it because I have also felt a vague annoyance with the fact that this news cycle develops in a thousand small drips rather than a single, steady stream of information.

As a reporter, it is my job to care about these things — and I’ve felt that way. I can only imagine where that leaves you. But some changes in golf are significant not for what they are but for what they represent. That’s the category the two changes filed on Tuesday morning fit into in the golf world: The PGA Tour’s expanded strategic alliance with the DP World Tour and Asian Tour; and the LPGA’s decision to play an event in Hawaii at what might be considered the best golf course on the islands, Nanea.

Golf.title: Cam Young's top tip for amateurs is one he still uses himself
Golf.summary: In this episode of Warming Up, Cameron Young explains that the most common advice he gives to amateurs is also the simplest. The post Cam Young’s top tip for amateurs is one he still uses himself appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Once you’ve caught the golf bug, you’ll try just about anything to get better. One week, it’s a viral swing drill. The next, you’re making practice swings in the living room or staying up late studying your favorite tour player’s swing on YouTube.

While it’s tempting to believe that one swing thought can change everything, the reality is that better golf is usually built on the less glamorous work. It’s a lesson PGA Tour pros understand better than anyone. While their swings may look effortless to us mere mortals, the game’s best players are constantly working on the basics. Just ask Cameron Young.

Here’s a truth most recreational golfers don’t want to hear: playing more rounds is not the same as getting better. Without understanding why your scores are what they are, playing more golf reinforces the same inefficiencies, round after round. That’s where golf statistics come in.

Golf.body:
ROCESTER, England – Ian Poulter has 17 career professional wins spread across 12 different countries. Surprisingly, he’s never won a pro tournament in his home country of England.

He has fellow Majesticks Golf Club Co-Captain Lee Westwood partially to blame. Poulter and Westwood entered the final round of the 2007 British Masters at The Belfry tied for second behind fellow Englishman Mark Foster. Westwood ended up winning the title with a superb final-round 65 while Poulter’s 70 left him in solo second.

Golf.title: A global golf shakeup has the Asian Tour partnering with the PGA Tour, DP World Tour—and leaving behind LIV Golf
Golf.summary: A global golf shakeup has the Asian Tour partnering with the PGA Tour, DP World Tour—and leaving behind LIV Golf Golf Digest
Golf.body:
Asian Tour CEO and Commissioner Cho Minn Thant says a new deal with the PGA Tour and DP World Tour will provide important pathways for his members. The Asian Tour is set to re-align with the DP World Tour and the PGA Tour in a formal partnership underlined by pathways and co-sanctioned tournaments, a move that means it will no longer act as LIV Golf’s important second tier.

The Asian Tour had partnered with LIV in 2021 before the league’s launch in 2022, when it created a lucrative group of tournaments called the International Series, which LIV golfers frequently teed up in. The series was central to the promotion and relegation element of LIV Golf, including the top two on its Order of Merit being promoted to LIV for the 2026 season.

Golf.title: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB
Golf.summary: Team Power Rankings: LIV Golf UK Presented by JCB LIV Golf
Golf.body:
Legion XIII is the hottest team entering this week, but there are plenty of others who are trending nicely as the action nears at JCB Golf & Country Club. As the LIV Golf League heads to JCB Golf & Country Club for LIV Golf United Kingdom Presented by JCB, the stage is set for the 10th stop on the schedule. Last year, Torque GC Captain Joaquin Niemann claimed the individual title with a three-shot victory over RangeGoats Golf Club Captain Bubba Watson, while Legion XIII took home the team trophy.

JCB Golf & Country Club will host the event for the third time. The par-72, 7,332-yard course opened in 2018 and was designed by Robin Hiseman. The 17th is the signature hole, a 255-yard par-3 that sits on a converted island and has the potential to play a crucial role when the leaders come down the stretch. If that wasn’t difficult enough, the 18th features a green heavily guarded by four intimidating bunkers, while the three-tier putting surface could see many players face difficult two-putts to finish their rounds.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I abandoned my lost ball — then found it in the hole! What now?
Golf.summary: What do you do if you give up on looking for your tee shot, only to later find it in the hole? Rules Guy has the answer. The post Rules Guy: I abandoned my lost ball — then found it in the hole! What now? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’ve got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. During a friendly 4-ball, teeing off on a blind par-4, my playing partner could not find her tee shot. The group searched for more than 3 minutes for her ball. My partner decided to “pick up” rather than head back to the tee. Soon enough, another player in the group checked the hole for fun — no one had thought to look there, since it was a par-4 … and there it was. A hole-in-one! But was it really, given the circumstances? – Teresa White, Purchase, NY

Really, it was, even if it sounds like the group didn’t get the free round of drinks owed at the 19th hole. Your partner indeed made a hole-in-one — and, even rarer, an albatross to boot! The fact that the ball wasn’t found in the search time didn’t matter, nor did her “picking up,” because she had already completed the hole. Rule 6.5, “Completing Play of a Hole,” completely covers this situation.

Golf.body:
Bryson DeChambeau has been accused of threatening to call Donald Trump during a row with senior R&A officials on Friday after the American golfer was handed a two-shot penalty at the Open.

DeChambeau’s alleged use of the US president’s name as he argued his case marks the latest bizarre turn in what was already the dominant story of the 2026 Open. DeChambeau was handed a two-stroke penalty for improving the line of his swing by standing on long grass behind his ball on Royal Birkdale’s fifth hole during round two. The 32-year-old argued his case furiously, including insisting upon returning to the scene of the incident with the R&A’s head of governance and a senior referee.

Over the past 24 hours, you’ve likely seen more than a few articles with those discovery-based headlines; hell, even this site wrote one. Golf.title: Cameron Young's patented pause? Here's why he does it
Golf.summary: In a recent episode of Warming Up, Cameron Young explained to Dylan Dethier the origins of his pause at the top of the backswing. The post Cameron Young’s patented pause? Here’s why he does it appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Cameron Young’s ball striking is perhaps his greatest asset as a golfer. Since graduating to the PGA Tour in 2022, the 29-year-old pro has ranked inside the top 35 in SG: Off the Tee every season and has twice ranked inside the top 15 in SG: Tee to Green. This season, as his putter has heated up to complement his lethal ball striking, he’s had a career year, winning the Players Championship and finishing top five in two majors.

Young’s swing is certainly effective, but it also comes with its own idiosyncrasies. Chief among them is the slight pause he makes at the top of his backswing. “I don’t feel it, obviously,” Young said in a recent episode of Warming Up. “It looks like it hangs there more than it does.”

A Tour player winning a tournament in a pair of spikeless shoes has become a rarity — let alone a major like the Open Championship, where you would think adverse weather and wet conditions require employing the extra traction that spikes provide.

In the latest episode of “The Deal” podcast with Jason Kelly and Alex Rodriguez, McGarity shared his insights on 8AM Golf’s business investments and strategy, and what he believes will drive the game’s future. Golf.title: How fast Fox trumped divisive DeChambeau to win Open
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox's pacy play set him apart from his peers as he triumphed at a fiery Birkdale that threatened to be overshadowed by Bryson DeChambeau's penalty, writes Iain Carter.
Golf.body:
Commentating on the thrilling climax of this year's Open, there was barely a moment to describe the biggest putt of Ryan Fox's life because he struck it so quickly. There were only 22 seconds between Sam Burns completing his final round and Fox stroking home the 11-footer on Royal Birkdale's 18th green. The putt made him champion golfer of the year.

It provided a magnificent and wholesome climax to the 154th Open, a dramatic championship marked by class and controversy. Bryson DeChambeau's two-shot penalty for trampling rough that improved the line of his swing path last Friday will not be forgotten. It was another incident that illustrated why he has become golf's most divisive figure.

Golf.body:
DeChambeau is close to Trump and classes him as a friend. DeChambeau celebrated his 2024 US Open success over McIlroy with the Trump family, and serves on the President’s Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition.

DeChambeau was in second place, one shot off the lead, before the penalty, but tailed away over the weekend to finish on four-under, in a tie for 14th, six shots off the winning score of Ryan Fox. DeChambeau, the two-time major winner, refused to address the media all week, but finally relented on Sunday evening when he spoke to Far and Sure, the golf website. Golf.title: Inside Cam Young’s 2 hours of belief … and 1 heartbreaking moment
Golf.summary: Cameron Young sat in the clubhouse and watched the Open Championship fall into his lap. In an instant it was snatched away. The post Inside Cam Young’s 2 hours of belief … and 1 heartbreaking moment appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
SOUTHPORT, England — Kyle Sterbinsky stood on the far left side of the Open Championship driving range and looked … warm. The sun seemed to canvas his entire face as he stared off in the distance at the big, golden leaderboard maybe 250 yards away. He couldn’t have been scanning the scene for info because his eyes were no longer useful. He and Cameron Young, the star golfer he caddies for, had reached those pregnant seconds when golf history is made. All they could do was listen.

There are two schools of thought that arise on Sundays at golf tournaments. Either you want to be the man in the house — shoes off, hat backwards, watching how your score holds up — or you want the ball and holes to play to beat the man in the house.

Golf.title: Pantomime villain Bryson DeChambeau ends his Open with a whimper | Sean Ingle
Golf.summary: Pantomime villain Bryson DeChambeau ends his Open with a whimper | Sean Ingle The Guardian
Golf.body:
Deep into the final round of the Open, and Bryson DeChambeau is almost legless in the last chance saloon. He has slipped to minus five, four off the clubhouse lead, with eight holes to play. Worse still, he has not made birdie all day. But there is a sliver of hope. After all, in 2017, Jordan Spieth made up four shots on the back nine here to take the Claret Jug. History couldn’t repeat itself, could it?

The loyal band of Brysonites cheer as he steps on to the tricky par-four 11th, and takes out a driver. Yet they, and Royal Birkdale’s infamous rough, are about to turn viciously against him.

Golf.title: Tommy Fleetwood's home Open had a different dream ending
Golf.summary: Tommy Fleetwood's dream home Open at Royal Birkdale didn't end with a Claret Jug. Instead, it closed with a scene that meant something deeper. The post Tommy Fleetwood’s home Open had a different dream ending appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Tommy Fleetwood has had a dream for his entire life. He has seen it when he’s closed his eyes, and he has envisioned it in quiet moments on and off the golf course. There’s a term for the space in between sleep and awake. It’s called hypnopompia, the state of near-consciousness in which dreams and reality blur, producing momentary lucid visions. Put simply, it’s a brief moment when you are living your dreams.

Tommy Fleetwood never fell asleep this week at his home Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. But he didn’t need to feel like he was living out a dream he’d long conjured in his mind. He just wasn’t sure how his dream would end.

Golf.title: Winners and Losers from 2026 Open Championship Sunday

Golf.body:
If you’re of the Ricky Bobby school of thought (if you’re not first, you’re last) you could come away from Royal Birkdale seeing just one winner and 155 losers. But we’re slightly more charitable than that — so let’s review a smattering of winners, losers and in-betweeners from what was (gulp) the final men’s major of the year.

Open champ Ryan Fox said in his post-win presser that he “sees things fast.” He plays that way, too: Quick, relentless, committed. As he said it: “It’s not that difficult to pick a shot and pick a club.”

Golf.title: Sam Burns' latest major close call hints at what's to come
Golf.summary: Sam Burns just wrapped up the best major season of his career, and all these close calls could add up to something special. The post Sam Burns’ latest major close call hints at what’s to come appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
SOUTHPORT, England — Sam Burns, Scottie’s bud. They play practice rounds together at all your better stops, speak the same language (golf, Southern, Southern golf), married young and had kids young. Burns, like Scheffler, is all church-on-Sunday, plus takeout shakes and whatever else is in the bag. You could see the two of them driving together to Brackenridge Park for the Texas Open, except that the tourney hasn’t been played there since Eisenhower was president. Scottie turned 30 on Father’s Day, last day of the U.S. Open. Burns turns 30 next week. They both seem about a decade short of playing in their first Senior British Open. Burns will be a lifer. You can just tell. According to the guy who won here Sunday night, Ryan Fox, he’ll be a major winner, too.

Burns would not have come here at all, to this posh nook of gritty northwestern England, but the missus, Caroline, pushed him out of the house and into a jet. He was talking about staying home, what with a new-born baby in the crib, in the Burns family home in a little town about an hour’s drive from Shreveport, La. “I’ve got this at home,” wife told hub. “Go over there and give it your best.”

DeChambeau was given a two-shot penalty after Friday's second round when he was judged to have inadvertently improved his swing path on the fifth hole.

Officials from the R&A, which organises The Open, said DeChambeau broke rules by trampling down knee-high rough behind his ball. The R&A emphasised that DeChambeau's actions had been accidental but pointed out that the rule still applied.

Golf.title: Why Ryan Fox was the perfect winner for a strange Open week
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox won the Open Championship, ending a strange and controversial week at Royal Birkdale with a good-guy winner. The post Why Ryan Fox was the perfect winner for a strange Open week appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
SOUTHPORT, England — Golf, it’s a beautiful thing. A year ago, the No. 1 player in the world went wire-to-wire at the Open Championship to claim a blowout victory. On Sunday, a little-known, 39-year-old PGA Tour lifer with just three career victories claimed his first solo lead of the week on the 72nd hole with a birdie putt for golfing immortality.

And best of all? He waited just 22 seconds to hit it. Ryan Fox was not the victor the scriptwriters had in mind for this 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. In fact, he might arrive in the winner’s circle as the most compelling evidence against the scriptwriters, beating out hometown kid Tommy Fleetwood and major-winner-in-waiting Cam Young and new-dad Sam Burns en route to his narrative-altering win.

Golf.title: Open fans provide valuable lesson with Bryson DeChambeau treatment
Golf.summary: Would Open fans give Bryson DeChambeau the same type of treatment Wyndham Clark received at the U.S. Open? No, not even close. The post Open fans provide valuable lesson with Bryson DeChambeau treatment appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
SOUTHPORT, England — You might have been wondering: Would Bryson DeChambeau be to this 154th British Open what Wyndham Clark was to the 118th U.S. Open, last month at Shinnecock Hills? You know, the player fans love to abuse?

This boils it down to the bone and then some, but if you’re looking at their original sins, there are similarities. Clark’s original crime was to bash in a locker at Oakmont Country Club, site of the 2025 U.S. Open, the premier annual event of the USGA. DeChambeau’s was stomping all over the deep fescue rough, right behind his ball, on the right side of the fifth hole, here at Royal Birkdale, site of this year’s Open Championship, premier annual event of the R&A. These were not acts, and these were not actors, out of the Bobby Jones/Jack Nicklaus Establishment Golfer playbooks. Like, the total opposite.

Golf.title: How Fox kept cool at baked Birkdale to win The Open
Golf.summary: Ryan Fox wins the Open Championship - his first major title - with his final putt on a record-breaking weekend at Royal Birkdale.
Golf.body:
As chaos unfolded on Sunday afternoon at the 154th Open Championship, Ryan Fox was the man who kept cool in the baking conditions at Royal Birkdale. The 39-year-old New Zealander, who is the son of All Black rugby legend Grant, shot a two-under 68 to finish one ahead of American Cameron Young and lift the Claret Jug.

After a final round full of spills and thrills, Fox knew a birdie on the 18th would be enough to secure his first major title. Easier said than done. Golf.copy:

Golf.title: Ryan Fox wins Open Championship, claims first major in shocking fashion
Golf.summary: New Zealand's Ryan Fox birdied the 18th hole at Royal Birkdale to win the 2026 Open Championship and claim his first major title. The post Ryan Fox wins Open Championship, claims first major in shocking fashion appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Cameron Young shot 64 on Sunday at Royal Birkdale, and then he waited. And waited. And waited some more. He started the day seven back but now held the clubhouse lead, although surely the hole he started in was simply too big a deficit to overcome and win the Open Championship, right?

But the longer he waited — it became over two hours — the longer it seemed like a possibility he would hoist the Claret Jug. The 39-year-old New Zealander, ranked 56th in the World, birdied two of his last three holes, including the par-4 18th, to clip Young by one and claim the biggest title of his career.

Golf.title: 2026 Open Championship money: How much every player made at Royal Birkdale
Golf.summary: 2026 Open champion Ryan Fox's winner's check will surpass what Scottie Scheffler received in 2025, with a payday of $3.2 million. The post 2026 Open Championship money: How much every player made at Royal Birkdale appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Last year, the Open Championship purse took a break from a steady annual uptick that began in 2017, opting to hold the line at $17 million. But this year, an increase is back. The 2026 Open Championship purse has gone up by $750,000 to $17.75 million.

Despite the record total, the Open Championship remains the least lucrative of the four major championships — and is even well below the PGA Tour’s Signature Event purses of $20 million. This year, the Masters and U.S. Open both offered $22.5 million to their fields, while the PGA Championship put up $20.5 million.

Golf.title: With major season over, Rory McIlroy's changing PGA Tour feelings take center stage
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy's major season ended with a whimper at the Open. With it wrapped up, his changing PGA Tour feelings now take center stage. The post With major season over, Rory McIlroy’s changing PGA Tour feelings take center stage appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy’s major season ended on Sunday with a whimper. The reigning back-to-back Masters champion shot a final-round one-over 71 at Royal Birkdale to finish in a tie for 40th at this Open Championship.

With his 2026 major season in the books, the six-time major champion looked to the future — but not with both eyes on the PGA Tour. “Look, this season feels very similar to last season,” McIlroy said. “Obviously won the first major of the year, fell off a little bit after that, but still any time you win a major in a year, you have to be pleased about that. Yeah, like I haven’t really took the time to enjoy that or celebrate that. Poppy’s got another four weeks off school until she goes back, sort of middle to end of August, so just going to enjoy the summer holidays with her and Erica. Yeah, that’s what I’m looking forward to the most.

Golf.title: Rory McIlroy Comments On Bryson DeChambeau As Performative At The Open
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy Comments On Bryson DeChambeau As Performative At The Open Forbes
Golf.body:
During Rory McIlroy’s Saturday press conference following his third round at The Open Championship, McIlroy was asked about Bryson DeChambeau’s two-shot penalty assessed after Friday’s round. “Yeah, look, I won’t pretend to be up here and defend Bryson,”, said McIlroy. “I’m not particularly fond of him. I think a lot of it’s performative. I think a lot of it’s for attention.

“To hold the tournament hostage like that, and to have all of us, players, volunteers, everyone waiting on him to depart, I didn’t feel like it was a great look.” McIlroy’s comments came after DeChambeau was assessed a two-shot penalty following Friday’s round. After his tee shot sailed right on the fifth hole on Friday, DeChambeau found himself in a penalty area in waist-high fescue grass. Instead of taking a drop, he elected to play his ball as it lay. However, as DeChambeau was lining up his shot, he stepped on and around the grass behind his ball. He struck the shot, ending up behind the green and eventually making a bogey on the hole.

Badminton.title: China Open: Liu/Tan Complete Unprecedented Treble
Badminton.summary: China Open: Liu/Tan Complete Unprecedented Treble BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Liu Sheng Shu and Tan Ning marked a watershed season at their home event VICTOR China Open 2026 on Sunday. The world No.1s etched their names into the history books after becoming the first women’s pair to capture three Super 1000 titles in a season since the HSBC BWF World Tour was introduced in 2018, sealing the milestone with a 21-14 21-19 victory over Yuki Fukushima/Mayu Matsumoto.

The triumph carried extra significance as the Chinese pair avenged their only defeat in a Super 1000 final, against the same Japanese duo at last month’s Indonesia Open. It also saw Liu and Tan emulate Wang Xiaoli/Yu Yang as the last home partnership to successfully defend the women’s doubles title in 2012, while extending China’s dominance in the event to a fifth consecutive edition.

Taipei, July 26 (CNA) Taiwan's Chou Tien-chen (周天成) on Sunday became the oldest winner of a Badminton World Federation (BWF) Super 1000 title after defeating France's Toma Junior Popov in the China Open men's singles final.

World No. 6 Chou beat world No. 16 Popov in a three-game match 21-15, 7-21, 21-13. Chou entered Sunday's match with a 1-2 career record in favor of Popov, though the last time the pair faced each other was in March, 2024.

Badminton.title: Popov makes French history
Badminton.summary: Popov makes French history Badminton Europe
Badminton.body:
SecondsToma Junior Popov produced the finest result of his career at Super 1000 level on Saturday, recovering from a slow start to defeat Canada’s Victor Lai 14-21, 21-12, 21-15 and become the first Frenchman to reach a men’s singles final at this level.

It was a performance built less on spectacle than adjustment. Lai controlled the opening game with his speed and directness, but Popov gradually changed the shape of the contest, extending the rallies, finding greater depth and forcing the Canadian to work harder for his attacking opportunities. By the deciding game, the Frenchman looked the more settled of the two and closed out a historic victory after another demanding three-game match.

Badminton.title: Top Underdogs to Watch at BWF World Championships 2026
Badminton.summary: Top Underdogs to Watch at BWF World Championships 2026 The News Mill
Badminton.body:
The BWF World Championships, set to take place in New Delhi from August 17 to 23, often witness unexpected upsets that reshape the badminton landscape. While established stars usually capture attention, emerging young players have previously seized opportunities to elevate their careers within a single tournament week.

According to a press release from the BWF World Championships, five underdogs stand out as potential surprise contenders at the 2026 event in India. Twenty-year-old Ayush Shetty from Karnataka has had a breakthrough year, emerging as one of India’s most promising men’s singles players. He secured his first BWF World Tour title by winning the 2025 US Open Super 300 and reached the final of the 2026 Badminton Asia Championships, defeating three top-10 players including Paris Olympics Silver Medallist Kunlavut Vitidsarn before earning the silver medal. Although the World Championships will be his first event featuring world-class opposition in every round, Shetty’s height and confident attacking play, coupled with home crowd support in New Delhi, may aid him in making a deep run.

Badminton.title: China Open: Chou Stops Shi Streak
Badminton.summary: China Open: Chou Stops Shi Streak BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Three years of frustration finally gave way to triumph as Chou Tien Chen ended a nine-match losing streak against defending champion Shi Yu Qi, battling to a 21-14 12-21 21-15 victory in the VICTOR China Open 2026 quarterfinals on Friday.

It was the Chinese Taipei veteran’s first win over top seed Shi since the team event at the postponed 2022 Asian Games in September 2023, and one built on an aggressive game plan designed to unsettle the home favourite.

Badminton.title: Ghana Badminton signs MoU with Special Olympics Ghana to promote inclusive sports
Badminton.summary: Ghana Badminton signs MoU with Special Olympics Ghana to promote inclusive sports Ghanaian Times
Badminton.body:
The Ghana Badminton Association (GBA) has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Special Olympics Ghana as part of preparations for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and Paralympic cycle.

The landmark agreement aims to strengthen collaboration between the two organisations by creating greater opportunities for athletes with intellectual disabilities to participate in badminton while expanding access to coaching, competitions, technical training, and athlete development programmes across Ghana.

Badminton.title: China Open: Tide Turned
Badminton.summary: China Open: Tide Turned BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Title favourites Wang Zhi Yi and Chen Yu Fei turned the tables on familiar foes to book their VICTOR China Open 2026 quarterfinal places on Thursday. Two-time defending champion Wang ended a three-match losing streak against Korean Sim Yu Jin with an assured 21-16 21-15 victory, keeping alive her bid to become only the second player in tournament history to win three consecutive women’s singles titles after Jiang Yanjiao (2008-2010).

Having struggled to find answers in their previous meetings, Wang was pleased with the way she stayed composed when the pressure mounted. “Every match is a new one. You’ve just got to stay in the moment, focus on what’s in front and think about tomorrow when it comes,” said the world No.2.

Badminton.title: China Open: Outsiders Steal Show
Badminton.summary: China Open: Outsiders Steal Show BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Wednesday at VICTOR China Open 2026 served a reminder that rankings sometimes count for little, as a trio of inspired performances sent fancied second and seventh seeds crashing out in Changzhou.

The biggest statement came from Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke, who produced his best victory in years to stun men’s singles second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn 21-13 8-21 21-19. The world No.30 held his nerve after the deciding game reached 19-all, sealing his first win over the Thai world No.2 in three years and his first victory against a top-five player since defeating then world No.4 Li Shi Feng at the China Masters in November 2023.

Badminton.title: China Open: Rescued by Resolve
Badminton.summary: China Open: Rescued by Resolve BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Three match points down and staring at another early exit, Weng Hong Yang found something that had been missing for much of 2026 – belief. The 2024 champion produced the comeback of the opening day, saving three match points at 20-17 before completing a thrilling 15-21 21-17 22-20 victory over men’s singles third seed Anders Antonsen in 84 unforgettable minutes at VICTOR China Open 2026.

It was a finish few inside the Olympic Sports Center Gymnasium saw coming. Weng had spent most of the afternoon chasing the Dane. After falling 11-6 behind in the opening game, he fought back to level at 14-all before Antonsen regained control. The Chinese player responded with a steadier display in the second game to force a decider but the momentum swung back heavily in Antonsen’s favour as he raced to a commanding 12-4 lead.

Badminton.title: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open
Badminton.summary: 'Importance of finding...': Virat Kohli’s one piece of advice helped PV Sindhu end her longest title drought and win a BWF Super 750 title in Japan Open The Economic Times
Badminton.body:
The 31-year-old shuttler won her maiden BWF Super 750 title at the Japan Open after defeating three-time world champion Akane Yamaguchi of Japan in straight games in the women's singles final in Tokyo on Sunday. The triumph marked Sindhu's biggest title since her historic BWF World Championships victory in 2019. Before this, her recent titles included the 2022 Singapore Open Super 500 and the 2024 Syed Modi International Super 300.

With the Japan Open win, Sindhu became the first Indian shuttler to claim the prestigious title and ended a title drought of more than two years. Sindhu's journey to the Japan Open crown was far from easy. The previous two years were among the toughest periods of her career. A stress fracture interrupted her progress, while her Paris Olympics campaign ended with an early exit.Repeated injuries and rehabilitation challenges made her comeback difficult. With every setback, the pressure surrounding one of India's most celebrated athletes continued to grow. However, Sindhu found a new perspective during a conversation with Virat Kohli, who himself has experienced the pressure of performing at the highest level.

Badminton.title: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov
Badminton.summary: Japan Open: Another Peak for Popov BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Christo Popov delivered a near-flawless performance to claim the DAIHATSU Japan Open 2026 to earn a morale-boosting title win ahead of the BWF World Championships next month. Koki Watanabe had had a draining three-game match against Yushi Tanaka in the semifinals, but to his credit, the home hope didn’t make it easy for the Frenchman, particularly in the second game. Watanabe had his chances in the second, but Popov’s greater sharpness and ability to last the rallies helped him nudge the tape, 21-11 21-19, for his third title of the year.

“This means a lot… it’s confirmation of what I was talking about for the last few months or weeks,” said Popov. “For me, it’s a very big achievement. Most of all, I like to play in Japan. I’m very happy to bring the title this year.

Badminton.title: PV Sindhu scripts history with Japan Open win, eyes BWF World Championships
Badminton.summary: PV Sindhu scripts history with Japan Open win, eyes BWF World Championships connectedtoindia.com
Badminton.body:
Two-time Olympics medallist PV Sindhu on Sunday, July 19, said that while she never stopped believing in herself, her victory at the Japan Open Super 750 reaffirmed that it is not over yet. The shuttler said she is now eyeing the upcoming BWF World Championships, scheduled to take place in New Delhi from August 17 to 23.

Sindhu’s win in straight games (21-17, 21-17) over Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi helped her clinch a first major title in two years, and she also became the first-ever Indian to win the tournament.

Competitor News.title: Topgolf Renews Partnership With First Tee To Grow Youth Golf Nationwide
Competitor News.summary: Topgolf Renews Partnership With First Tee To Grow Youth Golf Nationwide Dallas Express
Competitor News.body:
Topgolf announced Thursday the renewal of its longtime partnership with First Tee, the national youth development organization that uses golf to build character, confidence, and resilience in young people.

The Dallas-based sports and entertainment company said the renewed collaboration will continue leveraging its nationwide venues and First Tee’s programs to introduce more kids and teens to the game while fostering life skills.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Wholesale Manager
Competitor News.body:
Ritter Sport UK is accelerating its expansion across the convenience channel through a new permanent wholesale partnership with Parfetts, bringing five of its bestselling block chocolate flavours to all nine depots nationwide from this month.

The move forms part of Ritter Sport’s wider strategy to significantly grow its presence within the UK’s 50,000-strong convenience sector, making the brand more accessible to shoppers wherever they choose to buy chocolate. By increasing physical availability across convenience and independent retail, Ritter Sport aims to recruit new shoppers, build brand awareness and drive long-term category growth.

Competitor News.title: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership
Competitor News.summary: Ritter Sport UK accelerates its convenience expansion through nationwide Parfetts partnership Talking Retail
Competitor News.body:
Rum Raisin & Hazelnut, Marzipan, Milk Whole Hazelnut, Dark Whole Hazelnut and Pistachio will now be available to Parfetts’ network of 1,950 Go Local stores and more than 6,000 independent retailers, giving retailers access to one of the UK’s fastest-growing block chocolate brands while offering shoppers greater choice through premium-quality chocolate and distinctive flavour innovation.

The new permanent listing gives independent retailers the opportunity to differentiate their confectionery fixture with a brand that continues to outperform the wider market. At a time when consumers are eating less chocolate but demanding far more from every bite, Ritter Sport believes convenience retailers are well placed to capitalise on growing demand for products that deliver genuine quality, flavour and value.
